features.title: Package, content types and relationships
features.strategy: Open XML SDK on System.IO.Packaging. Parts are found through relationships, never by path; tolerate unusual part names, missing optional parts and external (linked) targets.
features.office: Verified: every corpus deck opens through its relationships, the password-protected ones too (generated/encrypted-agile and encrypted-standard 98.3 %).

features.title: Markup compatibility and extension lists
features.description: mc:AlternateContent, mc:Ignorable and the extLst/ext mechanism every newer feature uses.
features.strategy: Take the first mc:Choice whose Requires prefixes we implement, else mc:Fallback; honour mc:Ignorable. Dispatch a:ext and p:ext on their uri (a GUID) to the handler of the extension; skip unknown ones.
features.office: PowerPoint writes newer features twice: the new markup in mc:Choice (e.g. Requires="p14") and an older equivalent in mc:Fallback, e.g. p14 transitions fall back to p:fade, 3D models and zoom objects to a picture. Verified with the p14 transitions, a14 equations, cx charts and zoom objects of the corpus (generated/slideshow, charts-more, presentation).

features.title: Compatibility leftovers
features.description: Properties Office keeps for older versions or for converted VML content.
features.strategy: Not rendered; preserved for round-trips in the editor.

features.title: Encrypted and write-protected files
features.strategy: Password-protected files are OLE compound files with an EncryptedPackage stream ([MS-OFFCRYPTO], agile encryption): ask for the password and decrypt before parsing. Write protection only matters to an editor.
features.office: A password-protected presentation is a compound file ([MS-CFB]) with an EncryptedPackage stream that EncryptionInfo describes ([MS-OFFCRYPTO]). Agile encryption (version 4.4: spun SHA-1 to SHA-512 password hash, a package key sealed with it, AES-CBC in 4096-byte segments) and standard encryption (version x.2: AES-128/192/256 keyed by 50 000 SHA-1 spins, ECB) are decrypted with the password given to the converter; without one, Office's default password VelvetSweatshop is tried, and PasswordException tells a missing password from a wrong one. Write protection (p:modifyVerifier) and the read-only recommendation (p1710:readonlyRecommended) do not change how the presentation shows and only matter to an editor. Checked with generated/encrypted-agile (encrypted by PowerPoint) and generated/encrypted-standard (written by the fidelity tool, opened by PowerPoint).

features.title: Document properties
features.strategy: Metadata only; title, author and language go into the HTML head.

features.title: Custom XML parts
features.strategy: Not rendered; preserved for round-trips.

features.title: Object ids and co-authoring revisions
features.strategy: Not rendered. Stable creation ids help to match objects between slides (Morph) and in the editor.

features.title: Slide list and slide size
features.strategy: Slides in p:sldIdLst order. Sizes are in EMU (914400 per inch) and are rendered at 96 dpi, so the widescreen default 12192000 × 6858000 EMU becomes 1280 × 720 px; the viewer scales the slides to fit.

features.title: Hidden slides
features.strategy: Skipped in the slide show, shown dimmed in the overview.

features.title: Slide masters, layouts and slides
features.strategy: Draw the master's and the layout's non-placeholder shapes behind the slide's own shapes unless showMasterSp is off on the layout or slide; then the slide's shapes in document order.
features.office: Placeholders on layouts and masters are prompts for the editor and are never drawn on slides; only the slide's own placeholders are. Verified with generated/presentation (98.0 %); collapse, matchingName, preserve, userDrawn and showMasterPhAnim are editing state.

features.title: Placeholders and inheritance
features.strategy: Match a slide placeholder to the layout placeholder by idx alone (0 when missing), a layout placeholder to the master placeholder by type. Position, geometry, fill, line, body properties and list styles are inherited along that chain, property by property; the master's text style follows the type of the layout placeholder matched.
features.office: Measured with the object model on a Title and Content layout (placeholders of 24 type and idx combinations without positions of their own): slide placeholders match layout placeholders by idx alone, 0 when it is missing, whatever their types. p:ph without idx and with type body, dt, ftr, sldNum, pic or subTitle takes the title's place and title style; type title with idx 1 takes the content placeholder's place, size and bullets. A placeholder whose idx the layout lacks inherits from no placeholder at all, not even the master's of its type: it has no position, and only the master's text style of its own type applies (dt and sldNum at 18 pt, black and left-aligned instead of the master placeholders' 12 pt gray). The idx 4294967295 (-1) stands for none: such placeholders match by type (sldNum, ftr and dt take their layout placeholders' places at 12 pt gray, body the object placeholder's), and without a layout placeholder of their type the master's (on a blank layout, title and body take the master's places, while a title without idx or with idx 20 takes none). Verified with generated/presentation and text-basic; hasCustomPrompt, isPhoto and userDrawn are editing state.

features.title: Color mapping
features.strategy: bg1/tx1/bg2/tx2 map to dk1/lt1/dk2/lt2 through the master's clrMap or a layout or slide override.
features.office: The master's p:clrMap maps all twelve names (accents and hyperlink colors too), a layout's or slide's overrideClrMapping replaces it; a chart keeps its own c:clrMapOvr against the slide's mapping, for its text as well (measured with generated/colormap: dark mapping with swapped accents).

features.title: Slide background
features.strategy: The slide's background, else the layout's, else the master's. bgRef idx 1001 and above index the theme's bgFillStyleLst, lower values its fillStyleLst; the reference color replaces phClr.
features.office: Verified with generated/fills, colormap and presentation; bwMode, shadeToTitle and a15:backgroundPr only matter for black and white or legacy printing. Without a background on slide, layout and master the slide shows the color bg1 maps to (LibreOffice's layout-clrmap-override: a layout mapping bg1 to dk1 gives its slides a black background). A bgRef's picture fill names a picture of the theme part (Apache POI's themes deck).

features.title: Header, footer, date and slide number
features.strategy: p:hf flags on master, layout and slide decide whether the dt, ftr and sldNum placeholders are shown.
features.office: Only footer placeholders that exist on the slide itself are drawn; their slide number and date fields are recomputed when the slide is shown.

spec.title: Header/Footer information for a slide master

features.title: Sections
features.strategy: Group slides in the viewer's navigation; sections are not drawn.

features.title: Custom shows
features.strategy: Alternative slide sequences, selectable in the player and reachable through action links.
features.office: The player lists the custom shows and runs them from ppaction://customshow links (generated/slideshow).

features.title: Notes pages and speaker notes
features.strategy: Speaker notes text for the presenter view; full notes pages only for printing.
features.office: Speaker notes show in the presenter view with their levels, bold, italic, underline and links; notes pages (p:notesMaster, p:notesStyle) are a print layout and not rendered.

features.title: Handout master
features.strategy: Print layout only; not rendered.

features.title: Slide show settings
features.strategy: Loop, kiosk mode, slide range and pen color configure the player; print and web settings are ignored.

features.title: Editor view settings
features.strategy: Not rendered; zoom, guides and grid settings for the editor.

features.title: Tags and customer data
features.strategy: Not rendered; preserved for round-trips (add-ins store their data here).

features.title: Photo album, slide library and Designer metadata
features.strategy: Not rendered.

features.title: Theme color scheme
features.strategy: Twelve named colors; scheme colors in shapes resolve through the color map to these.

features.title: Theme fonts
features.strategy: +mj-lt, +mn-lt, +mj-ea, +mn-ea, +mj-cs and +mn-cs resolve to the major/minor fonts; the a:font entries choose fonts per script (Jpan, Hans, Arab, Hebr …) when the language of the run needs them.
features.office: Verified with generated/text-basic, text-eastasian and text-rtl.

features.title: Theme formats (style matrix)
features.strategy: Three fills, lines and effects (plus background fills) per theme, used through style references.
features.office: Verified with generated/fills, outlines and effects (style matrix references). Picture fills of the style matrix (textures in bgFillStyleLst) name pictures of the theme part or of a theme override, not of the slide (Apache POI's themes deck).

features.title: Shape style references
features.strategy: Resolve idx into the theme lists; the reference's color replaces phClr in the referenced style. fontRef supplies the default text color and theme font of the shape.
features.office: Shapes inserted in PowerPoint usually carry no direct fill or line but a p:style, so without style resolution they come out invisible or black. Verified with generated/geometry-presets, fills and outlines (inserted shapes carry only p:style). Fills and lines resolve level by level from the shape up through its layout and master placeholders, each level's own spPr before its own p:style: a slide title's style fill and line beat the master title's explicit noFill (Apache POI's customGeo deck).

features.title: Theme overrides
features.strategy: A layout or slide can override parts of the theme (usually the color scheme).

features.title: Object defaults, extra and custom colors
features.strategy: Defaults for new objects and color picker entries; only relevant to an editor.

features.title: Color models
features.strategy: Resolve to sRGB plus alpha. sysClr uses its lastClr, prstClr the named colors, scrgbClr is linear RGB.
features.office: Verified with generated/fills and colormap (99.7 %).

features.title: Color transforms
features.strategy: Apply in document order. lumMod/lumOff work in HSL, tint and shade most likely in linear RGB; every transform is to be checked against PowerPoint renderings.
features.office: Verified with generated/fills, colormap and smartart (theme color variations). gamma applies the sRGB gamma shift (encodes) and invGamma its inverse, so the gamma, shade, invGamma that converted PowerPoint 97 decks write shades in sRGB: 0066CC at 46.275 % is 002F5E (Apache POI's 45541 decks).

features.title: Shapes
features.strategy: Each shape is an absolutely positioned element with an SVG for geometry, fill, line and effects plus a text layer.
features.office: Axis-aligned rectangles and lines are drawn without antialiasing: every edge goes to the nearest pixel (fills and outlines at fractional positions), which crispEdges reproduces. p:sp/@useBgFill fills the shape with the slide's background, aligned to the slide (generated/colormap). bwMode only matters for grayscale printing. Verified across the corpus.

spec.title: Non-Visual Drawing Properties for a Shape

features.title: Names, alt text, hidden and decorative shapes
features.strategy: hidden="1" shapes are not drawn; descr and title become aria-label/title; decorative shapes get aria-hidden.

features.title: Position, size, rotation and flip
features.strategy: One CSS/SVG matrix per shape; rotation is in 60000ths of a degree, flips mirror around the center.
features.office: flipH does not mirror the text, flipV turns it by 180°.

features.title: Groups
features.strategy: Map child coordinates (chOff/chExt) to the group box and compose the rotations and flips of all ancestors into one matrix per leaf shape.
features.office: A locked canvas (lc:lockedCanvas in a graphic frame) is drawn like a picture of its DrawingML shapes: the box around them stretched over the frame together with their lines and text, shapes in groups counting by their own boxes mapped through their groups (docx/external/libreoffice/extras-ooxmlimport/ fdo43641: a group reaching past its rectangle and connector, 5.4 → 91.9 %), width and height swapped about their centers when turned by 45 to 135 degrees (or 225 to 315), as Office bounds groups (tdf143476_lockedCanvas_position: text turned by 308 degrees reaching exactly the top of its group's child space, 72.9 %), its own group transform unused, text without a font in Arial (generated/objects-more). a14:isCanvas and a15:nonVisualGroupProps only mark groups for editing. Verified with generated/transforms (99.3 %) and objects-more.

spec.title: Non-Visual Properties for a Group Shape
Non-Visual Properties for a Group Shape

features.title: Preset geometries
features.description: 187 preset shapes (rect, roundRect, arrows, callouts, flowchart symbols, stars …).
features.strategy: One formula engine evaluates presetShapeDefinitions.xml (adjust values, guides, paths) into SVG paths, so every preset comes from data instead of hand-written code.
features.office: The ECMA data file has no upArrow and lists upDownArrow twice (see the format catalog); upArrow has to be added and checked against PowerPoint. All 187 presets verified with generated/geometry-presets (99.3 %), upArrow from presetShapeSupplement.xml.

features.title: Custom geometry (freeforms)
features.strategy: The same formula engine. arcTo angles have to be converted to SVG arcs; path fill modes darken/lighten shade the fill; paths with their own w/h are scaled to the shape. Handles and connection sites are editor-only.
features.office: PowerPoint fills all paths of a geometry before it strokes any of them (measured with overlapping paths: the outline of the first path lies on the fill of the second, also for an outline-only path saved before a fill-only one); the document does the same where the order matters (presets chartPlus, chartStar, chartX, sketched shapes). In paths with their own w/h, arcTo angles are visual angles in the path's coordinates, before it is stretched to the shape (measured: clouds of other proportions than the 43200-unit square). Verified with generated/geometry-presets and sketched; adjust handles (a:ahXY, a:ahPolar) and connection sites are editor-only.

features.title: Connectors
features.strategy: Draw the stored geometry (straight, bent and curved connector presets with their adjust values); the editor recomputes routes only when connected shapes move.
features.office: Verified with generated/objects; a:stCxn and a:endCxn only matter when the editor reroutes.

features.title: Graphic frames
features.strategy: Container for tables, charts, SmartArt and OLE objects; dispatch on graphicData/@uri.
features.office: Verified with tables, charts, SmartArt, OLE objects and locked canvases in the corpus.

features.title: Locks
features.strategy: Editor-only.

features.title: Sketched outlines
features.strategy: The hand-drawn outline styles (curved, freehand, scribble) perturb the geometry with a seeded random function; matching PowerPoint needs its exact algorithm, a close look-alike is easy.
features.office: PowerPoint saves a sketched shape as the hand-drawn paths it derives from the original geometry and the seed: a custom geometry with an outline-only path (fill=none) followed by a fill-only path (stroke=0), and keeps the original geometry, the style and the seed (sd) in ask:lineSketchStyleProps in the outline's extension list. Opening a file it draws the sketch anew from those, which gives the saved paths again (checked through PowerPoint's own saved and re-exported decks), so the document draws the saved paths, fills before outlines, and lays out the text in the text rectangle of the original geometry (triangles and ellipses keep their inset text). A sketch on a preset geometry is dropped by PowerPoint, which then draws the sketch's original geometry (nothing if it has none); a sketch of the style none or without an original geometry leaves the custom geometry. Paths of a custom geometry that a third party saved with sketch properties but other than PowerPoint's are drawn as saved, while PowerPoint replaces them with its own (unpublished, seeded) sketch. Checked with generated/sketched (curved, freehand and scribble on five presets with text, without fill, with gradient fill, dashes, shadow, rotation and flips).

features.title: Sensitivity label markings
features.strategy: Shapes added by sensitivity labels; drawn like normal shapes, the marker itself is metadata.

features.title: No fill and solid fill
features.strategy: SVG fill color and opacity.

features.title: Gradient fills
features.strategy: SVG linear and radial gradients in the bounds of the geometry's filled paths (lin angle with scaled, rotWithShape); circle paths map to radial gradients, rect paths to four trapezoids, path="shape" to bands of the outline. Browsers interpolate in sRGB, so the engine adds intermediate stops computed in linear light.
features.office: Measured with gradient strips and PowerPoint's own EMF export: a two-color gradient (stops at 0 and 1) and a symmetric three-color gradient (A, B, A) use a GDI+ sigma bell blend (normal distribution CDF, sigma 0.25, normalized to 0 to 1) mixed in linear light; all other gradients interpolate linearly in sRGB. Rectangular path gradients are concentric rectangles from fillToRect to tileRect. Path gradients that follow the shape (path=shape) repeat the shape's filled outline in bands scaled from the tile rectangle to the focus rectangle, mixed in sRGB (measured with local/pathgrad: concentric ellipses, stars, triangles, hearts, parallelograms). 64 presets (block arrows, callouts with tails, ribbons, scrolls, waves, donut, moon, smiley face, sun …) draw such a gradient exactly as a circle gradient (measured: all 187 presets filled both ways; the binary format's fFillShadeShapeOK flag); custom geometries follow their outline. Every gradient spans the bounds of the geometry's filled paths rather than the shape's box (a block arc's band shows the whole gradient), and darkened or lightened paths shade the gradient's colors like a solid fill's (the faces of cans, cubes and bevels; local/pathgrad3: 99.2 %, local/pathgrad_all: 98.6 %). A gradFill without gsLst takes the stops of the style's gradient (fillRef) in its own direction (Apache POI bug 63200).

features.title: Pattern fills
features.strategy: The preset patterns as small SVG patterns in foreground and background color.

features.title: Picture and texture fills
features.strategy: SVG image clipped to the geometry: stretched into the fillRect insets, or repeated through an SVG pattern for tiles (offset, scale, alignment, flip).
features.office: Tiles are sized from the picture's own resolution; PowerPoint ignores blipFill dpi (measured). Verified with generated/pictures and fills; a:blip cstate (compression) does not change the picture. A shape's blipFill without stretch or tile is tiled at the picture's own size (LibreOffice tdf128596); pictures keep stretching. Slide backgrounds, group fills and table cells tile at the picture's own size too (LibreOffice tdf152070: a 300 dpi tile at 60 x 70 %).

features.title: Group fill
features.strategy: Use the fill of the parent group.
features.office: Verified with generated/fills.

features.title: Outline width and color
features.strategy: SVG stroke; widths are in EMU (12700 per point); inset alignment clips a doubled stroke.
features.office: Verified with generated/lines and outlines (99.0 %).

features.title: Dash styles
features.strategy: stroke-dasharray in multiples of the line width.
features.office: Preset dashes and custom patterns (a:custDash, a:ds: dash and space in thousandths of a percent of the line width) repeat in units of the line's width in whole pixels (measured: a 4 pt line, 5.33 px, repeats a 3:1 pattern every 20 px; a 1.5 pt line every 8 px). On a closed figure the pattern starts where the closing segment starts, the figure's last point, and runs through the closing segment first: a rectangle starts at its bottom left corner and runs up, a triangle at its bottom right corner, an ellipse at its left (measured with probe decks of one long dash on 24 presets and on freeforms); open figures start at their first point. Round caps lie within the dashes, and a round dash is at least one width long (a 0.5:2 pattern repeats every 3 widths); on closed figures the dashes cover [0, d) of the pattern, on open lines they lie half a width earlier, where the line's cap begins. Square caps do not cap the dashes, which end flat at their full length: only an open line's start gets the cap, and its end when it lies within a dash. Measured with generated/lines-dash (five custom patterns at 1.5, 4 and 8 pt on lines, rectangles and ellipses with flat, round and square caps): 89.7 %, the rest a pixel at the ends of the dashes and the drift of PowerPoint's curves along ellipses.

features.title: Joins and caps
features.strategy: stroke-linejoin, stroke-miterlimit and stroke-linecap.
features.office: Verified with generated/lines and outlines.

features.title: Arrowheads
features.strategy: Triangle, stealth, diamond, oval and open arrow heads as paths sized relative to the line width, with the line shortened under the head.
features.office: Heads are multiples of the line width but never smaller than a 2 pt line's (measured: medium heads 6 pt wide on lines of 0.25 to 2 pt, three widths beyond; LibreOffice's fdo47434). Verified with generated/lines (arrowhead types, widths and lengths).

features.title: Compound lines
features.strategy: Several parallel strokes or a stroke with a mask.

features.title: Gradient and pattern outlines
features.strategy: SVG gradient or pattern as stroke paint.
features.office: Gradient outlines take the gradient over the shape's box like fills (arrowheads too); pattern outlines draw the pattern itself, its 8 px tiles aligned to the slide like pattern fills (generated/outlines).

features.title: Effect lists
features.strategy: The effects of a list are applied in a fixed order; build one SVG filter chain per shape.
features.office: Verified with generated/effects (99.1 %) and effects-dag.

features.title: Outer shadow
features.strategy: SVG filter with blur (blurRad), offset (dist, dir), scaling, skew and alignment; CSS drop-shadow where it suffices.
features.office: A shadow is the shape scaled and skewed about its alignment point (algn, bottom center by default) with [sx, tan kx; tan ky, sy], the skew not scaled, then moved by dist along dir and blurred (σ = 0.35 blurRad). With rotWithShape 0, as PowerPoint writes its shadows, the offset and the transform stay on the slide, about the box around the turned shape (measured with generated/effects). Verified with generated/effects and probe/shadow, probe/rotshadow. The outline's outer half casts its shadow too (docx/external/libreoffice/extras-ooxmlexport/n705956-2: a 3 pt outline's shadow was cut at the box), and so does geometry beyond the shape's box (docx/external/libreoffice/extras-ooxmlexport/ tdf41466_testVmlShapeWithTextbox: a callout's tail 40 pt beside its box, 85.4 → 94.2 %).

features.title: Inner shadow
features.strategy: SVG filter inside the shape's alpha.
features.office: The shape's outside, blurred (σ = 0.35 blurRad) and moved against dir, colored and kept inside the shape; the filter region reaches beyond the shape by the distance and the blur so that the outside exists to cast it. Verified with generated/effects and local/innershadow (offsets 3 to 12 pt, blur 0 to 8 pt: 100 %).

features.title: Preset shadows
features.strategy: The 20 preset shadows as parameter sets of the shadow filters.
features.office: Verified with generated/effects.

features.title: Glow
features.strategy: Dilate and blur the shape's alpha, colored.
features.office: Verified with generated/effects. The glow grows from the shape's whole silhouette, also where its fill is mostly transparent (Word's PDF of LibreOffice's extras-ooxmlexport/fdo66688: a 5 pt glow around a white fill of 20 % alpha as strong as around an opaque one, 86.7 → 99.9 %).

features.title: Soft edges
features.strategy: Erode and blur the alpha mask.
features.office: Verified with generated/effects.

features.title: Reflection
features.strategy: Mirrored copy with distance, blur and a gradient alpha mask.
features.office: The copy is scaled and skewed like a shadow about algn, moved by dist along dir, faded along fadeDir (90° by default) across the copy from stA at stPos to endA at endPos and blurred; with rotWithShape 0 the turned shape is mirrored on the slide (measured with generated/effects). Verified with generated/effects and probe/refl.

features.title: Blur and fill overlay
features.strategy: SVG Gaussian blur; fill overlay blends a fill over the shape.
features.office: Blur: a Gaussian blur with sigma = rad / 3 (measured); without grow the result is cut at the outline's outer edge, with grow it spreads beyond. Fill overlay: the overlay fill is blended over the shape's fill only, not its outline (over, mult, screen, darken, lighten as CSS blend modes in an isolated group).

features.title: Effect containers (effect DAG)
features.strategy: Effect graphs with containers and blends; rare outside themes from Office 2007.
features.office: PowerPoint draws an effect graph instead of the shape (measured with generated/effects-dag, 97.2 %): its input is the whole shape with its text; a container of type sib draws its children's outputs over each other, type tree feeds each child the previous output; an empty container draws nothing, while a graph without any effect leaves the shape as it is. a:effect ref brings in the fill, the line, fill and line with the text (fillLine), or a named container's output. Every effect outputs only its own result: an outer shadow or glow without the shape, a reflection without the original, alphaOutset grows the alpha with black, fill paints the input's alpha (gradients through a mask), relOff and xfrm move it, the color effects work as on pictures. blend draws its container's output over the input in a blend mode, over being overlay (measured to two levels), mult multiply and so on; fillOverlay likewise with a fill. Drawn as nested SVG groups, filters, masks and mix-blend-mode.

features.title: 3D scene (camera and light)
features.strategy: The camera turns and projects the shape: a CSS matrix3d for the front face with its text, SVG polygons for the body. The light rig lights every face with Lambert diffuse and Phong highlights, fitted per rig.
features.office: Measured on generated/three-d: the presets' angles and fields of view (30 cameras, corners within 0.4 pt; the eye stands 907.5 pt / 2 / tan(fov / 2) in front of the shape); oblique presets shear by 0.3 of the depth (legacy ones 0.5), legacy perspective presets by 0.133 per axis. Legacy oblique cameras with a rotation of their own turn the scene before they shear it, their light rig staying with the viewer under the turns about the horizontal and vertical axes and turning along in the picture plane (LibreOffice's Scene3d_legacyObliqueBottomRight 51.5 to 97.3 %, Scene3d_lightRig_legacyCamera 41.2 to 98.4 %); how modern oblique cameras turn is not measured yet (Scene3d_obliqueTopRight). All 27 light rigs were fitted on extruded cubes, cylinders and tilted bevels rendered in two base colors (rms below 0.03, brightRoom 0.05); dir turns a rig in 45° steps clockwise, a:rot turns it further. sp3d z moves the shape along its own axis (perspective enlarges it, turned cameras shift it). Shadows and glow of 3D shapes come from the body's back as the camera sees it (the glow half as wide), soft edges do not apply. A backdrop (a:backdrop) takes the shadow and glow instead: the flat shape's picture lies in that plane with its x along up × normal and its y along the up vector, its corner at the anchor less half the shape's size (scene coordinates as DrawingML's: y down, z towards the viewer), the shadow moved by its distance along the scene's x and y, behind the body when the plane lies behind it, else over its sides (fitted to glow and shadows on walls and floors of both orientations with perspective and isometric cameras within 3 px; local/backdrop, backdrop2, backdrop3: 98.3 to 98.6 %). The shape's text casts its shadow there too, over the shape's own and darker where they overlap, as its plain glyphs without effects of their own (local/bdtext: a floor plane shows the text in the shadow).

features.title: 3D shape (bevel, extrusion, material)
features.strategy: Bevels (top and bottom, measured profiles), extrusion, back face and contour are built as SVG polygons, sorted back to front and lit with the rig and the material; the front face is drawn by the camera.
features.office: Measured on generated/three-d: bevel profiles from edge-on silhouettes (they scale with width and height independently; a bevel is at most half the smaller side wide); the front face lies in the shape's plane, the top bevel's outline its height behind it, then the extrusion and the bottom bevel. The shape's line is part of the body: the body reaches to the line's outer edge, the sides take the line's color unless extrusionClr is set, and so do the outer band of the bevels and of the back. The contour is an unlit tube of contourW (black by default) around the rims, creases and silhouettes; a face coming towards the eye covers all but r·cos α of its inner half, and the body moves back so that the tube does not reach in front of the shape's plane. Materials were fitted against threePt, the latest on cubes from 25 sides on black and gray slides (local/cubes-*, within 1 to 3.5 levels rms): matte without highlights, plastic and metal with stronger and tighter ones, metals partly tinted, the legacy materials' and the powders' from the half vector; metals, dkEdge, softEdge and the powders fade towards the silhouette, metals, softEdge and the powders whiten there ((1 − n·v)^3.8 for metal and softEdge), powder mixes half white into the surface color; flat ignores the light's direction; legacyWireframe draws every mesh edge, hidden ones included. clear and translucentPowder are translucent, the same in every channel: clear most transparent facing the eye (opacity 1 − 0.9 n·v), translucentPowder towards the silhouette (0.7 n·v); only faces towards the eye are drawn, the highlights add in full (the color brightens by highlight / opacity and saturates at white) and text on the front face stays opaque (local/clear, clearA-C). Without a body (no extrusion, bevel or contour) the powders show warmMatte's light with their broad highlights only, no pastel look and nothing towards the silhouette (local/powder, matflat1-2). Pictures and gradients keep their texture on the bevel.

features.title: Pictures
features.strategy: SVG image with crop (srcRect; negative values pad) and the shape's geometry as clip path.
features.office: Verified with generated/pictures (99.5 %). A picture without its picture (an a:blip naming none, or a part the package lacks) shows PowerPoint's sign: a 1-pixel #6D6D6D frame on its edge, the broken-picture icon 6 pixels in and "The picture can't be displayed." in Office's language ("Das Bild kann nicht angezeigt werden."; Apache POI's missing-blip-fill, LibreOffice's tdf147586); the player words it in the viewer's language.

features.title: Raster image formats
features.strategy: PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP, SVG and WebP natively (also when the package names another content type); TIFF decoded (strips or tiles; uncompressed, PackBits, LZW, Deflate with prediction, CCITT group 3/4, JPEG; bilevel, gray, palette, RGB(A), CMYK; 1-16 bit) and converted to PNG, JPEG-compressed TIFF merged into one JPEG (Huffman re-coding where strips use different tables); color profiles carried along; JPEG XR decoded by our own decoder after ITU-T T.832 (spatial and frequency order, tiles, all overlap modes, 4:2:0, 4:2:2 and 4:4:4, gray, CMYK, n-channel, 1 to 32-bit integer, fixed and floating point, RGBE, interleaved and separate alpha, orientation) and converted to PNG.
features.office: PowerPoint keeps TIFF pictures as inserted (also CCITT and JPEG compressed ones) and honors embedded ICC profiles (PNG, JPEG, TIFF; verified with a swapped-primaries profile); profile-less CMYK shows through a 9^4 table measured from PowerPoint's rendering (harvest-cmyk). Pattern tiles of stretched pictures reach a margin with the edge pixels repeated, so edges no longer blend with the opposite edge. Inserted .jxr/.wdp pictures stay JPEG XR, but PowerPoint names .jxr parts image/png (the extension's default), so pictures are told apart by their bytes. The JPEG XR decoder matches Windows' own (WIC) sample for sample on 44 files of its encoder in all its options (frequency and spatial order, tiles, overlap 0-2, subsampling, quality, without flexbits, highpass or lowpass, separate and interleaved alpha, rotations; gray, bilevel, 565, 555, 101010, 16-bit, float, CMYK): the highpass prediction direction comes from the lowpass coefficients before dequantization (the order of steps in 9.4 would take them after), centred chroma is upsampled with the taps (-2, 9, 28, -3) / 32 (4:2:0 in both directions before one rounding), packed formats swap red and blue unless RED_BLUE_NOT_SWAPPED. Only WIC's own 8-bit conversion of 10-bit, 16-bit and floating point samples differs by 1 at most. hdphoto parts of artistic effects (a14:imgLayer) are originals; the blip holds the rendered result. Deck: picture-formats 99.9 % (slide 2: ten JPEG XR pictures). The bytes count, not the name: a PNG stored as .emf (image/x-emf) shows as the PNG (LibreOffice's graphic-stroke).

features.title: EMF and WMF pictures
features.strategy: Our own EMF/EMF+/WMF interpreter that emits SVG ([MS-EMF], [MS-EMFPLUS], [MS-WMF]).
features.office: EMF and WMF are frequent in real decks (icons, content pasted from Excel or Visio, older charts). The interpreter draws the GDI records (lines, curves, PolyDraw, shapes, paths, regions, clipping with OffsetClipRgn and meta regions, world and page transforms, text, BitBlt, StretchBlt, MaskBlt, PlgBlt, DIB transfers, AlphaBlend, TransparentBlt, gradient fills, hatch and pattern brushes in output pixels) and the EMF+ records of dual and EMF+ only files (fills and outlines with solid, hatch, texture, linear and path gradient brushes, paths, regions, images, strings, driver strings, containers, transforms, clips). Logical palettes are played: CreatePalette, SelectPalette, SetPaletteEntries, ResizePalette and AnimatePalette, PALETTEINDEX colors and DIB_PAL_COLORS bitmaps against the selected palette (the default one has the 20 static colors), PALETTERGB as its own color (local/palette, EMF and WMF). Monochrome pattern brushes (EMF CreateMonoBrush, WMF DIBCREATEPATTERNBRUSH with BS_PATTERN) paint in the text and background colors as GDI does, not in their palette's black and white (measured with the previews of ActiveX toggle buttons and scroll bars, whose dithers PowerPoint draws in the control's colors). A bitmap's negative width or height reaches from its origin the other way, its first column or row at the origin, as in GDI's StretchBlt (LibreOffice's tdf149206: an EMF named .wmf whose screenshot sits 750 x -600 under a window turned upside down, 29.2 to 83.5 %). EMF text aligned by its top or bottom (TA_TOP, TA_BOTTOM) stands by GDI's ascent and descent of the font realized in whole pixels of the metafile's device (lfHeight -ppem): the VDMX record of the size for the Windows ANSI character set, else usWinAscent and usWinDescent scaled and rounded (measured with GDI's GetTextMetrics: Arial, Times New Roman, Courier New, Segoe UI and Verdana by their VDMX, Calibri and Cambria rounded, Tahoma's VDMX for all glyphs not used; Word's PDFs: Arial at 13 px 13 px below the reference point, Calibri at 15 px 14 px, LibreOffice's tdf99631 in Word 89.4 → 98.8 %; PowerPoint: poi/at.ecodesign.www_downloads_Vertiefungsvortrag_elektronik slides 21 and 25 0.4 and 1.6 points better). WMF text keeps the unrounded ascent (not measured). 8-bit text reads in its font's character set: Cyrillic (204) as Windows-1251, Central European (238) as 1250 and so on, symbol fonts byte by byte, the rest as Windows-1252 (Word's PDF of LibreOffice's fdo58949: Equation.3 previews with lfCharSet 204 print "НВВ", 83.9 → 95.8 %). Flood fills are not drawn, as PowerPoint draws none (measured); escapes draw nothing, color management records leave the colors as they are, and OpenGL records are not drawn. Verified with generated/metafiles (PowerPoint's EMF and WMF exports, GDI+ dual and GDI-only recordings, GDI records: 96.2 %; hatches come out smoothed in Chromium where GDI sets whole pixels).

features.title: SVG pictures
features.strategy: Use the SVG part; the surrounding a:blip holds a PNG fallback.
features.office: Verified with generated/pictures.

features.title: Picture color effects
features.strategy: SVG filters (feColorMatrix, feComponentTransfer) or pre-processing in C#. Recolor presets (grayscale, washout, duotone with theme colors) and transparency (alphaModFix) are the common ones.
features.office: clrChange matches the alpha too unless useA is 0. Verified with generated/pictures.

features.title: Artistic effects and picture corrections
features.strategy: Draw the main blip.
features.office: PowerPoint saves the processed picture as the main blip and keeps the original in a14:imgLayer, so the effect is already baked in.

features.title: Audio and video
features.strategy: HTML5 video/audio with the picture's blip as poster image; trimming and fades in the player; caption tracks as WebVTT.
features.office: Bookmarks (p14:bmkLst) travel with the media element and start the trigger sequences that wait for them (p14:bmkTgt, evt onMediaBookmark); caption and subtitle tracks (p173:tracksInfo) become WebVTT text tracks of the video; a file's declared media type (contentType) is kept. CD audio (a:audioCd with its a:st and a:end track times) cannot play from a document. Online videos (a:videoFile linked to a web player such as YouTube's embed page) play in a frame that loads the player only when it plays; YouTube refuses to play in a page opened from a file (error 153), so the presenter app serves the document over localhost. Verified with generated/media (99.4 %).

features.title: OLE objects, ActiveX controls and signature lines
features.strategy: Draw the fallback picture stored with the object.

spec.title: Global Element for Embedded objects and Controls

features.title: Ink
features.strategy: Use the mc:Fallback picture first; later draw the InkML traces as SVG paths with pressure-dependent width.
features.office: Ink (p:contentPart, Office 2010 markup chosen over the fallback picture) is drawn from its InkML or InkActionML part (strokes an action removed left out): the smallest trace coordinates go to the part's top left corner; a part as large as its points plus the last brush's width (its natural size, as PowerPoint writes it) keeps the ink's scale, any other size stretches the points to fill it; stroke widths never scale; a part with a highlighter (rasterOp maskPen) is half transparent as a whole. With a pressure channel (F) the width follows the pen: (0.25 + 1.5 F/max) times the brush width, tapering smoothly between points, ignorePressure keeps the brush width (measured with generated/ink). fitToCurve: PowerPoint draws such a stroke as cubic Beziers fitted to its points, one piece for up to five points, with corners where the fit breaks (a stroke following the pen's pressure as a polyline through the points moved onto that curve). It is drawn here as the uniform cubic B-spline of the points with its ends held: approximating like PowerPoint's fit, corners cut inwards, no loops or overshoots; reversals stay corners. Along dense ink both stay within half a pixel of the polyline; on sparse points PowerPoint's fit reaches further (a three-point V keeps its depth, a zigzag of five becomes one U; local/inkfit, inkfit2-4). Verified with generated/ink (98.8 %) and probe/ink.

features.title: 3D models
features.strategy: Show PowerPoint's picture of the model (mc:Fallback); while the slide show animates the model, our own glTF 2.0 reader and WebGL2 renderer (model3d.js, only in documents with models) draws it on a canvas over the picture, lit and tone mapped like PowerPoint.
features.office: PowerPoint stores the model as GLB (am3d:model3d r:embed) with a rendered picture of it (am3d:raster, Office3DRenderer, 2 px per point, also the mc:Fallback picture). The camera (pos, up, lookAt in EMU, 36,000,000 EMU to the meter) looks at the model; a perspective's fov spans the square objViewport (viewportSz) about the frame's center, of which the frame shows its middle, and nothing is drawn outside that square. The model's transform: model units to meters (meterPerModelUnit), preTrans, scale, rotation about x, then y, then z (60000ths of a degree), postTrans. Lighting, measured with generated spheres and mirror balls: a studio environment (a room with windows, reconstructed from the mirror balls) for diffuse light and reflections (split sum, GGX), the slide's point lights (candela, inverse square, linear scRGB colors) and its ambient light; emissive counts half; base color factors are kept in 8 bits; the result goes through PowerPoint's tone curve (s = 1 - exp(-(2.358 u^0.666 + 1.886 u)) per channel, u in the units in which an unlit material shows its base color). Our renders of calibration spheres and boxes are within 1 to 5 of 255 on average; contact shadows (ambient occlusion) are not drawn.

features.title: Cameo and live camera feeds
features.strategy: Show the stored picture; a live camera (getUserMedia) only in the player.

features.title: Picture sources and formulas
features.strategy: Not rendered; the picture itself is stored as usual.

features.title: Text body and text box
features.strategy: The text box is the geometry's text rectangle minus the insets (default 91440 EMU left/right, 45720 top/bottom); anchoring top, middle or bottom, anchorCtr, wrap or no wrap, rotation and overflow.
features.office: anchorCtr centers the smallest box around the text, the paragraphs keep their alignment within it; vertOverflow ellipsis and clip drop the lines that do not fit whole (ellipsis ends the last line kept with …, whole words removed) and the rest is anchored as usual; horzOverflow clip cuts at the text rectangle, not at the insets; spcFirstLastPara keeps the space before the first and after the last paragraph; compatLnSpc shows no difference (measured with generated/text-body). Compatible line spacing (compatLnSpc) leaves PowerPoint's lines where they are (measured: 150 % spacing unchanged); forceAA only asks for anti-aliasing. A text area narrower or lower than its insets collapses to its middle, x + (w + lIns - rIns) / 2 (measured with the object model: a box 5 pt wide with insets of 10 and 2 pt sets every line at 6.5 pt whatever its alignment; a box 1 pt high 0.5 pt below its top). A placeholder 0 wide does not wrap (one line in footer, body and title placeholders), while text boxes, shapes and placeholders 1 pt wide wrap every character (LibreOffice's 0-width-text-wrap). Verified with generated/text-body (97.7 %), text-more and objects-more.

features.title: Autofit
features.strategy: Apply the stored fontScale and lnSpcReduction; with spAutoFit the stored shape size already fits the text.
features.office: PowerPoint saves the shrink factors it computed when the slide was last edited; recomputing them yields different line breaks than PowerPoint shows. Without stored factors it does not shrink at all, even when normAutofit is inherited and the text overflows (verified with generated/text-basic, slide 5). The scaled sizes are whole points, halves rounded up: 26 pt at 90 % is laid out at 23 pt and 25 pt at 23 pt, 18 pt at 62.5 % at 11 pt (the object model reports these sizes; generated/text-more, slide 5). Verified with generated/text-basic, text-body and text-more.

features.title: Paragraphs
features.strategy: Alignment (left, center, right, justified, distributed), margins, first-line or hanging indent, levels 0–8.
features.office: fontAlgn t, ctr and b line up the tops, middles or bottoms of runs of different sizes (base and auto: the baselines; measured with generated/text-body). A word longer than the line breaks between characters, and its trailing spaces hang at the end of its last piece as after any word (measured: "縦書き 2024年 AB" in mongolianVert columns one character long takes no column for its spaces, generated/text-more slide 3). Verified with generated/text-body, text-rtl and text-eastasian.

features.title: Line and paragraph spacing
features.strategy: Line spacing as a percentage of the line height or in points; space before and after.
features.office: Measured with the text-metrics calibration deck (9 fonts, multiples, exact spacing, sizes): single line height is 1.2 × the font size for every font, multiples scale it, exact spacing is rounded to whole points. At single spacing the baseline sits at 1.2 × size × ascent/(ascent+descent) (typo metrics if USE_TYPO_METRICS, else Windows metrics); above single spacing at H × min(0.75, ratio); below at max(S × ratio − (S − H), H × min(0.75, ratio)). Lines take the largest ascent and descent of their runs; bullets do not count. Space before is ignored for the first paragraph; percentages of space before/after refer to 1.2 × font size. Glyph origins are snapped to device pixels. Verified with generated/text-metrics (98.9 %).

features.title: Tab stops
features.strategy: Left, center, right and decimal tabs, default tab size from defTabSz.
features.office: Tab stops (a:tabLst, inherited through the list styles like the other paragraph properties) are measured from the text area's left edge, the origin of marL: left stops put the text there, center stops center it, right stops end it there and decimal stops put its decimal point there (text without one ends at the stop); text never moves left of where it already is; past the last custom stop the default stops continue at multiples of defTabSz; a hanging first line (negative indent) stops at the margin first. Measured with generated/text-tabs (default spacings, every stop kind, margins and indents, bullets, centered and right-aligned paragraphs). A tab binds to the word after it: a word that does not fit after the tab's stop takes the tab to the next line, and a tab that starts a line keeps what fits of the word after its stop, possibly nothing (measured with the object model's lines in a 385 pt line of 20 pt Arial: "Text⇥after" with a stop at 380 pt gives "Text", a line with only the tab and "after …"; with a stop at 350 pt "Text", "⇥afte", "r …"; a stop past the line's end leaves the tab alone on its line; a second tab moves to the next line with its word and stops at the first stop there).

features.title: Bullets and numbering
features.strategy: Bullet glyph in its own font (Wingdings and Symbol mapped to Unicode or embedded), color and size; automatic numbering in 40 schemes (arabic, roman, alphabetic, circled, East Asian, Hebrew, Arabic, Thai …) with startAt; picture bullets.
features.office: A hanging indent reaching left of the text area moves the paragraph right (marL 0, indent -27 pt: bullet at 0, text at 27 pt). With a first line indented further than the margin the bullet stays at the margin and the text starts at the indent (object model: marL 0 and indent 27 pt start the text at 27 pt; marL 36 and indent 0 right after the bullet; LibreOffice's bullet-indent). Numbering continues while the paragraphs before at the level count in the same scheme from the same start, and begins anew with another scheme or start (LibreOffice's n90255: 3 4, II III, C D, iv v, f) g) for pairs of paragraphs with five schemes). Latin letters repeat after z (aa, bb); Arabic schemes count in hijā'ī (arabic1) and abjad (arabic2) order followed by a hyphen-minus; Thai letters skip ฃ ฅ ฆ. Picture bullets are as high as the capitals and sit on the baseline. Verified with generated/lists (all 41 numbering schemes, picture and character bullets).

features.title: List styles and the text style cascade
features.strategy: Run → paragraph → the shape's lstStyle → layout placeholder → master placeholder → the master's title or body style → the presentation's defaultTextStyle; the shape's fontRef adds color and font. Text outside title and body placeholders skips the master's other style except for its color.
features.office: Measured with the object model, otherStyle level 1 at 10 pt bold red Courier New right-aligned with 150 % spacing and defaultTextStyle at 30 pt italic blue Georgia centered with 80 %: text boxes, shapes and dt, ftr and sldNum placeholders without a layout placeholder take size, italics, font, spacing, alignment, indent and line spacing from defaultTextStyle and only the color from otherStyle (not its bold); table cells take otherStyle. LibreOffice's TextOnCircle (otherStyle 15.12 pt, defaultTextStyle 18 pt) rises from 43 to 93 %. Verified with generated/text-basic, text-body and presentation.

features.title: Runs and character formatting
features.strategy: Size (hundredths of a point), bold, italic, all caps and small caps, single and double strikethrough, superscript and subscript (baseline %), character spacing, kerning threshold, highlight.
features.office: Superscripts and subscripts are drawn at two thirds of the size, raised or lowered by the baseline percentage of the full size (measured). Equalized character height (normalizeH) stretches every glyph's ink from the baseline to the font's ascent (OS/2 usWinAscent; measured: all letters of 32 pt Calibri 40 px tall, descenders lifted); kumimoji keeps digits upright in vertical text. A line break's own size (a:br a:rPr) sizes its line only when the line has no other text: a 60 pt break after 20 pt text leaves the line 24 pt high, alone it makes it 72 pt (generated/text-more, slide 4). A paragraph's own default run properties (a:pPr/a:defRPr) format its runs before the list styles do (POI's bug63290: a run without properties in the paragraph's red 40 pt). altLang, bmk, dirty, err, noProof, smtClean and smtId are editing state. Verified with generated/text-basic, text-underline and text-more. Underlines and strikethroughs run on through the spaces between words, not through spaces ending a line (POI's aascu deck: 'Math Problem Solving' in one piece). A presentation without p:defaultTextStyle (as other programs write them) takes PowerPoint's own, which kerns from 12 pt (LibreOffice decks with Calibri text: kerned without any kern attribute).

features.title: Fonts per script
features.strategy: Choose the latin, East Asian or complex-script font per character; resolve theme fonts; see engine.fonts.
features.office: PowerPoint draws every missing font in Calibri, whatever its panose, pitch family or charset say (measured with serif, monospaced, script and decorative hints in generated/text-body). Some names that are no family's still find one (160 names measured against the installed fonts, in this order): a style word run on is dropped (TahomaBold: Tahoma, regular); a name beginning with Arial, Helv, Times, Courier, Segoe, Palatino or Lucida Console takes Arial, Arial, Times New Roman, Courier New, Segoe UI, Palatino Linotype or Consolas whatever follows (ArialMT, TimesNewRomanPSMT, SegoeUI); a trailing " Bold" or " Italic" sets the style (Cambria Bold); a hyphen ends the name (Georgia-Bold: Georgia, regular). The free families Liberation Sans, Liberation Serif and DejaVu Sans (also DejaVu Sans Mono) take Arial, Times New Roman and Verdana when they are not installed; Liberation Mono, DejaVu Serif, Arimo, Tinos, Carlito and Caladea do not (measured by line widths; LibreOffice's 3d_rotated_text). Other names, also PostScript names such as CambriaMath, become Calibri (generated/text-more, slide 7). Characters inserted from symbol fonts (stored at U+F000 to U+F0FF) take the run's symbol font (a:sym): Wingdings 1 to 3, Symbol and Webdings render with their own glyphs (generated/text-more). charset, panose and pitchFamily only help find substitutes; fonts are resolved by name. Verified with generated/text-basic, text-eastasian, text-rtl and text-more.

features.title: Embedded fonts
features.strategy: Decode the font parts back to TrueType with our own Embedded OpenType and MicroType Express decoder (EOT header, LZCOMP with its adaptive Huffman trees, Compact Table Format to glyf, loca, cvt, hdmx and VDMX); lay text out with them where the family is not installed and carry them in the HTML as @font-face.
features.office: PowerPoint stores every style of an embedded family (p:regular, p:bold, p:italic and p:boldItalic, also styles the presentation does not use) as a part of type application/x-fontdata: Embedded OpenType version 0x00020002 with the subset and compressed flags, without XOR. The subset keeps the glyph ids and holds the glyphs of the characters the presentation uses and of printable ASCII; the other glyphs are empty. A family that is installed is taken from the system. Decoded, the kept glyphs' outlines and programs, hmtx, cmap and hdmx equal the installed fonts and VDMX is byte for byte the same (14 faces of Georgia, Comic Sans MS, Consolas and Segoe Script); Chromium's font sanitizer accepts the rebuilt fonts. generated/text-fonts, converted with its embedded fonts in place of the installed ones, renders pixel for pixel like with the installed fonts (95.0 %, the usual gap of small text). A variable font is embedded as the same file for every style (seen with Wix Madefor Display, wght 400 to 800): the slide show draws bold at the Bold instance (wght 700) and kerns it from GPOS (see engine.textLayout), while Slide.Export draws such text in Arial, so slide exports of decks with embedded variable fonts are no references.

features.title: Text fill and outline
features.description: gradFill, blipFill, pattFill and a:ln inside run properties.
features.strategy: SVG text paint or glyph outlines from our layout engine for gradient, picture and outlined text.
features.office: Gradient and pattern fills span each line separately (from the line's start to its end and from its ascent to its descent); the outline is centered on the glyph edge and drawn over the fill. Verified with generated/text-effects.

features.title: Underlines
features.strategy: The 18 underline styles drawn by our layout engine with position and thickness from the font.
features.office: All 18 underline styles: the post table's underline position is the line's top, the thickness its own rounded to whole pixels; dashed styles repeat in units of that thickness (dotted 1:1, dash 3:2, long dash 7:4, dot dash 3:2:1:2, dot dot dash 3:2:1:2:1:2), heavy ones are twice as thick, reaching up from the plain line's bottom, with the same pattern; double ones are two lines of three quarters of the thickness, the second above the first; wavy ones are waves four thicknesses long. An underline line of its own (a:uLn) outlines the plain underline, which is filled with a:uFill (or the text's color): the line lies half inside and half outside the edges, at least a pixel, with its own dash (measured with Arial 40 pt and uLn of 0.25 to 6 pt: 0.25 pt adds a row of line above and below a fill of three rows, 2 pt leaves one row of fill between three rows of line, from 3 pt the line covers the fill); uLnTx and uFillTx follow the text. Small text drawn by the browser gets the style, color and width as CSS. Measured with generated/text-underline (every style in the text color and in a color of its own, lines of their own, runs of different sizes): 76.1 -> 90.7 %, the rest one-pixel rounding of the line's position.

features.title: Text effects
features.description: effectLst on runs (shadow, glow, reflection, soft edges).
features.strategy: The shape effect filters on the glyph layer, sized with the line's largest font; scaled and skewed shadows as transformed copies about the shape's box; reflections mirrored line by line; warped WordArt text gets the same filters.
features.office: PowerPoint sizes text effects with the largest font of each line, unlike a shape's (measured with probe decks of 8 to 240 pt lines in several fonts, in exported slides and in the slide show alike): outer shadows (distance and blur) and glow grow with (size / 78 pt)^0.695, inner shadows with size / 117 pt, a reflection's blur with size / 79 pt and its distance with size / 14.5 pt. A reflection mirrors each line about its baseline: the distance extends the mirrored box below the baseline by half the scaled distance and the fade runs over that box. Text glow is dilated by 0.46 r and blurred by r / 6 at the outer scale. Verified with generated/text-effects.

features.title: Fields
features.strategy: slidenum and datetime1–13 are computed when rendering; other field types keep their stored text.

features.title: Text columns
features.strategy: The text is laid out at the column width and its lines are shared out over the columns.
features.office: A column takes the lines that fit the text area's height, but at least an even share of all lines, and the last column the rest (measured with the object model, nine boxes of 4 to 12 lines in 2 and 3 columns: 7 lines in 2 columns 5 lines high are 5 and 2, 3 lines high 4 and 3; 12 lines in 3 columns 5 lines high 5, 5 and 2, 3 lines high 4, 4 and 4; 33 lines in three columns overflowing 11, 11 and 11). So an auto-sized box keeps all its text in the first column (LibreOffice's auto-height-multi-col-shape). Verified with generated/text-body.

features.title: Vertical and rotated text
features.description: a:bodyPr/@vert (vert, vert270, eaVert, mongolianVert, wordArtVert), @upright and @rot.
features.strategy: Rotate the line layout, or lay out top to bottom for East Asian and WordArt vertical text.
features.office: vert and vert270 lay the text out along the shape's height and turn it by 90 or 270 degrees; the insets stay with the shape's sides and the anchor works across the turned lines (the text's top faces right for vert, left for vert270). eaVert keeps ideographs, kana and full-width forms upright (turned back about the middle of their em box) and stacks lines right to left; mongolianVert stacks them left to right. wordArtVert stacks upright characters in columns from the left (wordArtVertRtl from the right): characters and columns 1.41 x the size apart, the baseline 1.12 x the size into each cell, words that do not fit break between characters, trailing spaces take no room (measured). rot turns the laid-out text, vertical text too, about the middle of the text rectangle (LibreOffice's tdf149551: 12 degrees, 60 -> 70 %). upright keeps the text level in rotated shapes, laid out with width and height swapped between 45 and 135 (225 and 315) degrees. Table cells (tcPr vert) wrap at the row height (generated/text- vertical).

features.title: WordArt transforms
features.strategy: Glyph outlines from the font, bent along the warp's guide paths (41 presets) into SVG paths.
features.office: The text's ink box fills the envelope between each pair of guide paths (glyph tops on the upper path, baselines on the lower one), measured in arc length. Lines are shared out among the envelopes in order (textButtonPour: two lines take the upper and the middle one, four lines two, one and one; empty paragraphs count), and all envelopes share one scale each way (measured with probe decks of H strokes, residuals under 0.5 px): along, the envelope whose ink is longest for the middle of its envelope (the mean of its two paths' lengths) fills it and sets the scale, the others' ink taking its part where the alignment puts it; across, the tallest ink fills its envelope and the others' is centered at that scale, a line without ink counting with its line box (a line of A's before an empty paragraph keeps 0.56 of its envelope's height) (local/warp-buttons 61.5 to 88.8 %; LibreOffice's tdf139618_WordArtBitmapFill, textDeflateInflate, 65.6 to 80.7 %). Presets with one or three paths put every glyph rigid on the path at its middle, at the glyph's size and placed by the line's alignment; the lines are shared out among the paths alike (textButton: one line on the upper arc, two on the arc and the middle line, three on all three, four with two on the upper arc; empty paragraphs count), and such text is not wrapped (a line longer than the text box stays whole on the lower arc). Text from old WordArt (fromWordArt) is scaled evenly to the path's length (measured with textArchUp in generated/text-body). Verified with generated/text-effects (WordArt transforms). Every line follows a parallel of the path, a line pitch apart, on the side away from the box's center: on a circle or an arch up the last line lies on the path and the others outside it, under an arch down the first line lies on the path and the others below. Glyphs are spaced by arc length on their line's parallel, from the parallel's start or as aligned (insets do not count), and then lowered: the line on the path has its baseline 0.79 em under the top of its line box below the path (eight fonts, 12 to 72 pt, within 0.01 em; 4.8 px under textButton's middle line in 24 pt Aptos). Other text shrinks when it is longer than PowerPoint measures the path: an arc counts its width radius times its sweep, as if it were a circle (textArchUp with eight H's: 177.6 px a radian on arches of 10 to 40 degrees with a width radius of 180 px, 91 px with one of 90 px), so that text runs on along the ellipse past the ends of an arch flatter than that circle; a line longer than its parallel is centered on it (LibreOffice's tdf116350-texteffects 69.1 to 73.5 %). Known deviations: old WordArt with several lines on part of an elliptic arc comes out larger than in PowerPoint (LibreOffice's tdf125573); on an arch down of an ellipse PowerPoint places the glyphs closer to the path's start, by a factor of its arc length that depends on the ellipse (0.98 at 360 x 267 px, 0.977 at 360 x 133, 1.007 at 180 x 267, none on a circle), and textCircle on a circle at some start angles (0.982 at the default 180 degrees and at 210, none at 181, 195, 240 and 270; at 12 and 24 pt, radii of 67 and 133 px alike), for which no rule is found.

features.title: 3D text
features.strategy: scene3d/sp3d on the text body; same approach as 3D shapes.
features.office: A scene of the text body's own (a:bodyPr/a:scene3d, a:sp3d; Format Shape, Text Options) gives the glyphs a body while the shape stays flat: the glyph outlines are extruded, beveled, backed and contoured like a 3D shape's (extrusion in the text's color unless extrusionClr), the text itself is the front face inside the top bevel, lit like it, and the scene turns about the center of the glyphs, not of the shape (measured). A bevel wider than half a glyph stroke is cut at the ridge with its height in proportion; PowerPoint shades such ridges somewhat differently (thin beveled text looks lighter there). Text in a 3D-turned shape turns with the shape's front face; a:flatTx keeps it out of the scene, facing the viewer at the shape's place (measured). Small 3D text is drawn from its outlines too (LibreOffice's 3d_rotated_text: 18 pt text turned a quarter, 41.6 to 91.4 %). Checked with generated/text-3d (97.1 %): extruded and beveled under a legacy perspective, turned only, beveled in a shape, extruded in a color of its own, flat text.

features.title: Equations
features.strategy: OMML laid out with the OpenType MATH table of Cambria Math (another installed math font otherwise, the mc:Fallback picture when there is none): runs in the math alphabets (m:sty, m:scr), fractions (bar, skewed, linear, stacked), scripts and pre-scripts, radicals, n-ary operators, stretchy delimiters with separators, matrices, equation arrays, accents, bars, group characters, limits, functions, boxes, border boxes and phantoms, spaced by TeX's atom classes. An equation is an inline object of the text layout, drawn as glyph outlines under transparent selectable text.
features.office: Measured against PowerPoint with probe decks at 18, 20 and 40 pt: display equations reach at least the math font's ascent and descent and stand MathLeading below the top of their line; display operators take the first size at least 1.5 x DisplayOperatorMinHeight tall; fractions keep their size in display equations (text style below the top level) and shrink inline; delimiters take the smallest size at least twice the content's reach from the axis less 630 units (between 613 and 645 by the sizes chosen), and a delimiter with separators sets its parts in text style; skewed fractions put the fraction slash (U+2044) in the largest size within their ink; accents keep their size over one character and grow to the largest size within a wider base; an n-ary operand follows a thin space less what the display size adds to the italic correction, at least SpaceAfterScript after limits beside it; hidden limits keep their baselines; empty arguments keep a 0.9 em placeholder; m:vertJc of a group character picks the part on the baseline (top when missing). PowerPoint's exports cut off accents stretched over several characters and narrow stretched group characters; that is not imitated. Verified with generated/math.

features.title: Right-to-left and complex scripts
features.strategy: Bidi algorithm (UAX 9) in our layout engine, complex-script fonts, rtl paragraphs and columns.
features.office: Measured with generated/text-rtl: paragraph levels follow pPr rtl, not the text (UAX #9 weak, neutral and implicit rules); a neutral between text of two directions takes the direction of its run's language (a:rtl, else lang) — PowerPoint keeps the space of a de-DE run 'PowerPoint ' with it in an Arabic paragraph and mirrors a bracket of a Hebrew run. Right-to-left paragraphs start on the right: left margin, indent and bullet are measured from the right edge, the bullet reads right to left ('1.' shows as '.1'), alignment l and r stay absolute; justified lines stretch their spaces. Right-to-left runs are shaped right to left (HarfBuzz mirrors brackets) and drawn whole by the browser below 30 pixels per em. Tabs in lines with right-to-left text count their width only; right- to-left tables and columns see table.structure and text.columns.

features.title: East Asian typography
features.strategy: Kinsoku line breaking rules, East Asian line breaking and hanging punctuation, ea fonts, vertical text.
features.office: Measured with generated/text-eastasian: with the kinsoku rules (pPr eaLnBrk, on by default) a line does not start with closing punctuation or small kana and does not end with an opening bracket; hangingPunct (on in PowerPoint's default text styles) lets 、。，． hang past the end of the line instead of pushing the character before them down (Latin punctuation never hangs: a line whose closing period would pass the end moves down with its word, external/libreoffice/sd-data/ TextFittingComparisonWithMSO_1 and _2); eaLnBrk 0 turns the rules off, lines then break between any East Asian characters, punctuation included, and nothing hangs; latinLnBrk breaks Latin words anywhere to fill a line. PowerPoint ignores the presentation's own kinsoku characters (p:kinsoku). Korean breaks at spaces.

features.title: Table grid and merged cells
features.strategy: Lay out the grid ourselves (column widths from gridCol, merged cells from gridSpan, rowSpan, hMerge, vMerge) and position the cells absolutely; an HTML table would compute its own sizes.
features.office: Row heights (a:tr/@h) are minimums; PowerPoint grows rows to fit their text. A right-to-left table (tblPr rtl) mirrors its cells with their left and right borders, not the text in them (generated/tables). Verified with generated/tables (97.7 %); a:headers and a:header only name cells for accessibility. The table's effects (a:tblPr/a:effectLst) are cast by the cells' fills and borders, not the text; translucent fills show the shadow through (LibreOffice's table-shadow-blur); a scaled shadow is scaled about its alignment point like a shape's (tdf150020-shadow-alignment: 130 % about the center).

spec.title: Header Cells Associated With Table Cell

features.title: Cell formatting
features.strategy: Margins, anchoring, vertical text, fills and borders including diagonals; shared borders resolved like PowerPoint.
features.office: tcPr anchorCtr centers the cell's text block; bodyPr wrap none and horzOverflow have no effect in cells, the text always wraps (measured with generated/tables). Beveled cells (a:cell3D, also from the style's tcStyle) are drawn as shapes with a top bevel seen from the front: the bevel's strips and the face lit by the cell's light rig (three-point from the top by default) and material (plastic), the fill on the face inside the bevel (generated/tables-more: circle, angle and relaxed inset bevels, faces lighter under the three-point rig). Verified with generated/tables and tables- more.

Top-Left to Bottom-Right Border Line Properties

features.title: Table styles
features.strategy: Combine whole table, banding, first/last row and column and corner cells in PowerPoint's order for the flags set in tblPr. PowerPoint draws only its 74 built-in styles, so we need their definitions, harvested from PowerPoint itself.
features.office: PowerPoint draws tables only in its 74 built-in styles, looked up by a:tableStyleId; the definitions in ppt/tableStyles.xml are not used for drawing (measured with patched decks): a built-in id draws the built-in style whatever the file defines under it (Apache POI's table-with-different-font-colors, 93.1 to 98.6 %), and a style of the file's own, even an exact copy of a built-in one under another id, or an inline a:tableStyle draws No Style, Table Grid (POI's bug68703, a Google Slides style, 61.2 to 97.5 %). The 74 styles as PowerPoint writes them into ppt/tableStyles.xml are kept as a resource (generated/tables-more slide 2: six styles with an empty style list, 98.4 %). Verified with generated/tables and tables-more. A table without tableStyleId is drawn in No Style, Table Grid, not in the presentation's default style (measured with a patched deck; Apache POI's table-with-no-theme).

features.title: Chart part and settings
features.strategy: Read chart settings and render from cached data; print settings are ignored.
features.office: A chart's c:clrMapOvr replaces the slide's color mapping for the chart, text included (generated/colormap). The chart area's corners are rounded unless c:roundedCorners says otherwise; PowerPoint rounds them where the element is missing too, by 9.8 pt whatever the chart's size (measured with local/rounded: 200 x 150 to 300 x 450 pt). Blank cells (c:dispBlanksAs) show as gaps where the element is missing, as zero where it says so or names nothing, or spanned by the line without a marker (generated/charts-data). Labels of values beyond the axis are hidden as PowerPoint writes c:showDLblsOverMax 0 (8 and 11 on an axis up to 6 go unlabelled). Dates of the 1904 system (c:date1904) are moved to the 1900 one. Print settings (c:printSettings, header and footer, page setup) and editing state (c:protection, c:userInterface, c:externalData) do not change the picture. Verified with generated/charts, charts-more, charts-details and charts-data.

spec.title: Legacy Drawing for Headers and Footers

features.title: Series and data caches
features.strategy: Series values, categories (multi-level), number format codes; filtered series stay hidden.
features.office: Verified with generated/charts-data (multi-level categories, blanks, hidden rows; filtered series, kept in c15:filtered* outside the series list, stay hidden).

features.title: Bar and column charts
features.strategy: Clustered, stacked and 100 % stacked bars as SVG rectangles.
features.office: Negative bars of a series that inverts them (c:invertIfNegative) take the fill of c14:invertSolidFillFmt, else white, with a black hairline where the series has no line of its own (measured with generated/charts-details). Verified with generated/charts, charts-details and charts- data.

features.title: Line charts
features.strategy: Polylines with markers; smoothed lines need Office's Bézier construction.
features.office: Verified with generated/charts and charts-data (smoothed lines: interior segments as PowerPoint's, the end segments a little off). A line chart without the c:marker flag shows markers on series without a marker of their own (LibreOffice's tdf105517).

features.title: Pie and doughnut charts
features.strategy: Arcs as SVG paths; pie-of-pie and bar-of-pie with series lines.
features.office: Pie of pie and bar of pie (c:ofPieChart): the split (splitType pos with splitPos, 2 by default; val, percent, cust with c:secondPiePt) moves points to a second pie or a stacked bar beside the main pie, which shows them as one slice formatted by the extra data point and centered towards the second plot; the second plot is secondPieSize % of the main pie high, a bar half as wide as high; the gap at gapWidth 100 is 0.514 (pie) or 0.259 (bar) of the main pie's diameter; the second pie's slices start (clockwise) where the combined slice ends, the bar's first point on top; series lines (c:serLines) join the combined slice's edges to the second plot's top and bottom. Measured with generated/charts- details: 0.06 -> 0.97 on that slide. Verified with generated/charts, charts- details and local/pielabels. A fill of the series' own colors the points without one even where the colors vary by point (LibreOffice's tdf150176 and tdf146756: the first slice in bg2). The room for outside labels follows the series' label position, not single points' (centered labels with some at bestFit keep the pie at full size: tdf125444, percentage-number-formats); with them the pie is 0.876 of half the plot's smaller side less 0.163 of the labels' size across (Word's PDFs of LibreOffice's extras-layout/tdf137116: 53.71 pt of 63.0 at 10 pt, outside_long_data_label 59.0 of 69.0, tdf134866 99.25 of 115; local/pielabels slide 4: 142.5 of 163.5; tdf137116 79.2 → 94.3 %, outside_long_data_label 81.9 → 99.6 %, pielabels 98.9 → 99.2 %). Word keeps that room wherever a series has data labels at all, even ones that show nothing (c:dLbls of every show* 0; scratch/WordProbes/probe_pielabels.py on LibreOffice's extras-ooxmlexport/tdf123873: 64.7 pt in radius with the flags alone or with text properties, a separator or point entries, as with values shown, 75.5 pt without c:dLbls; tdf123873 84.4 → 97.0 %). A plot area placed by hand around the pie (layoutTarget inner) holds the pie with its series' explosion; single exploded slices reach beyond it (tdf146756_bestFit, tdf146487).
