Pie of Pie or Bar of Pie Type

features.title: Area charts
features.strategy: Filled SVG polygons, stacked or 100 % stacked.
features.office: Verified with generated/charts and charts-more.

features.title: Scatter and bubble charts
features.strategy: Value axes on both sides; bubble size by area or width.
features.office: The largest bubble measures 0.2307 m + 2.65 pt (m = the smaller side of the plot area before the axis labels; measured through COM) times bubbleScale; sizes by area or width. The value axes grow until every bubble fits (data plus radius in axis units, then the usual 5 % headroom), which reproduces PowerPoint's scales; bubble legend keys are round. bubble3D is drawn flat.

features.title: Radar charts
features.strategy: Polar axes as SVG.
features.office: One spoke per category clockwise from 12 o'clock; the value gridlines are polygons, the value axis line is drawn as every spoke and its labels stand along the first spoke (1.14 s - 1.25 pt left of it); the category axis draws neither line nor gridlines. The radar is centered in the plot area with radius min(W/2 - (widest label + 0.3056 s - 3.005), H/2 - (L + 0.3127 s - 5.248)), measured through COM with 25 layouts. Category labels stand 6 pt beyond their spoke, left- or right-aligned at the sides and centered above and below. The value axis ends at the first major unit from the largest value, without the 5 % headroom of other charts (measured: 7.9 on 0 … 8, 9.6 on 0 … 10); charts without style part draw spokes only where the axis has a line of its own.

features.title: Stock charts
features.strategy: High-low lines and up/down bars over line series.
features.office: High-low lines join each category's lowest and highest point, up/down bars run from the first to the last series (category width / (1 + gap width)) and cover the lines; the series lines are usually invisible. A dot marker is a circle half the marker size. Legend entries of series without a line keep the narrow square-key width and show only their marker.

features.title: Surface charts
features.strategy: Contour bands in 2D; 3D surfaces with chart.threeD.
features.office: Contour (top view) charts: the band scale is the value axis without headroom; the surface is a top view of a 3D box whose sides are proportional to the category and series counts, 97.3 % of the inner plot area. Each grid cell splits along the diagonal with the larger value sum; facets are lit with 0.52 + 0.595 n·l (light from the upper right at 31 degrees; facets turned away keep darkening) plus a specular highlight; the top view's box is 0.6 × its base high, scaled by the inner plot area's height over its width (measured with tilted planes in square, wide and tall charts, local/contour: within 2 levels). 3D surfaces (meshes cut into the value bands, drawn back to front by their grid cells) and wireframes (band-colored grid and contour lines) are drawn with chart.threeD. Contour charts verified with generated/charts-more; 3D surfaces see chart.threeD.

features.title: Axes, gridlines and number formats
features.strategy: Reproduce Office's automatic minimum, maximum and major unit; number formats need an Excel number-format engine; date axes, logarithmic and reversed scales.
features.office: Measured: zero is included unless all values lie in the top sixth of their maximum; the maximum gets 5 % headroom; with a fixed maximum and an automatic minimum the ticks count down from the maximum (700000 over data down to -479325: -700000 … 700000); the major unit is the smallest 1-2-5 step giving at most ten intervals, each at least 1.1 line heights tall; 100 % stacked axes are exactly 0 to 100 %. Built-in format 14 ("m/d/yyyy") shows the locale's short date. Numbers and dates take the system's regional format, not the chart's language (c:lang; measured: an en-US chart shows 2,5 on a German system); the converter takes it as an option, the current culture by default. Category labels that do not fit their slots wrap at the slot's width where every word fits it, else all rotate by -45 degrees (local/catwrap-horizontal: two- to six-word labels wrap, also in a chart 200 pt short; one word wider than its slot turns all labels); date axes that label as many dates as fit show all of them, wrapped, where their words fit (LibreOffice's bnc889755), and built-in format 17 (mmm-yy) reads "Okt 12" on a German system. Rotated labels sit with the end of their middle line at the category; in Word's charts labels turned up by -45 degrees are boxes whose top right corner sits on the category, the first category their width across from the outer edge, the last their line's height up from the right one (agent AK in Word's PDFs: powertools/CU004-Chart-Cached-Data-04 87.8 → 98.0 %, libreoffice/extras-ooxmlimport/tdf82824 90.1 → 98.8 %); labels of an axis crossing inside the plot area stay at the axis. Display units (c:dispUnits: built-in or custom) divide the value labels, and their label (c:dispUnitsLbl) shows its own text or the unit's name in the chart's language (German Office: Millionen, x 10000), turned a quarter beside the labels with its end at the top of the plot area, in a column of its own. Category axes label every tickLblSkip-th category and mark every tickMarkSkip- th, their labels keep lblOffset % of the default distance; numeric categories (dates on a date axis) take the axis's number format, months abbreviated as Office does (German: Mrz, Jun, Sep). A plot area placed by hand (c:manualLayout) still turns category labels that do not fit by -45 degrees. Horizontal value axes divide the plot area's width before the labels beside it take their room into intervals of at least four font sizes, however wide their labels are, which then overlap (measured: bar and scatter charts 150 to 900 pt wide with 9 and 12 pt labels; Office 2016 charts keep one label wide plus three font sizes). Category labels beside a vertical axis (bar charts) wrap at half the outer plot area's width less half the first and half the last value label, keep the lines that fit their category's height with an ellipsis after the last (centered without it), and stand as blocks as wide as their longest line beside the axis, their lines centered (measured: bar charts 200 to 950 pt wide with 9 to 24 pt labels and value labels of several widths or none; local probes). In Word category labels of a horizontal axis turned a quarter by their own rotation (bodyPr rot ±5400000) wrap at half the outer plot area's height, their lines centered on each other, the block's middle at the category (docx/local/tlb-*, tlc-*: a Calibri 9 label beside charts 150 to 550 pt high and 288 or 432 pt wide breaks where a line would pass half the height less 10.1 to 12.7 pt; LibreOffice's extras-layout/xaxis-labelbreak 22.8 → 92.6 %). A plot area placed by hand wraps them at half the chart's width less those overhangs and keeps all labels inside the chart: it moves left until the value label at its right edge is 6 pt inside, then gives up width on the left to the labels beside it (LibreOffice's tdf48041: 60.8 to 90.2 %). Not yet: the plot area of narrow bar charts whose labels nearly fill their categories starts lower in PowerPoint. Multi-level categories (c:multiLvlStrRef) put every outer level in a row of its own, the label gap below the categories, each name centered over its group with lines along the group edges from the axis through the row; with c:noMultiLvlLbl the names join their group's first label as further lines. Labels may hold line breaks and align in their slot (c:lblAlgn l, r: flush with its edge). Date axes (c:dateAx) count days, months or years from the first date to the last (c:baseTimeUnit, else by the closest dates), every point in the slot of its date, empty units keeping their place, labels every major unit (c:majorUnit in c:majorTimeUnit) or as many as fit (generated/charts-data: 1, 4, 5, 12 January on a day axis, 1 and 15 January sharing January). Days without a major unit whose dates do not fit label every day, every second or every seventh, the first that fits, flat, turned by 45° (slots of 1.73 line heights) or, for days and second days, by 90° (1.18 line heights), else the first of every month, the slots taken on the plot area's width for flat labels (local/da-*: 20 to 200 days on 181 to 829 pt axes, the same in Word; docx/external/powertools/CU004 57.7 → 87.8 %, libreoffice/extras-ooxmlimport/tdf82824 49.8 → 90.0 %). Known deviation: below labels turned by 45° PowerPoint's plot area is up to 5 pt narrower on each side than ours. Lines and areas run on through the dates without data between their points (dispBlanksAs only concerns blank cells). A plot area placed with its labels (layoutTarget outer) holds them all: half a value label at the top, the first turned category label at the left edge. Category labels stand (1 + lblOffset / 100) / 2 default gaps below the axis (measured with offsets of 0, 200, 400 and 1000). Display unit labels stand 3.6 pt beside the value labels in a column 9.5 pt wider than their line, their end 2.5 pt below the top of the plot area. Horizontal value axes keep each interval one label and three font sizes wide (a 418 pt scatter axis up to 9 steps by 2). Checked with generated/charts-data, charts-details (99.2 %) and a label offset probe (99.6 %). The sides of category and value axes follow the chart type whatever c:axPos says: a bar chart's category axis is vertical (LibreOffice's tdf48041 saves it at b, PowerPoint shows the categories on the left).

features.title: Data labels
features.strategy: Label text from values, categories, series names, percentages or cell ranges; automatic placement and leader lines.
features.office: Data labels wrap at a fifth of the chart's width, box, insets and legend key included; a word longer than a line breaks between characters (measured: 'Wwwwwwwwww; 1' reads 'Wwwwwwwww' and 'w; 1'). The default separator is a line break between a percentage and a name shown without the value, else the list separator of the chart's language and a space ('One; 40' with a German Office). Pie labels, measured against PowerPoint's label boxes for pies turned in 5 degree steps (local/pieangles, local/piebestfit, local/pielabels): ctr at half the radius; inEnd centered on the middle ray where the ray leaves the label 3.7 % of the radius inside the edge; outEnd with the inner edges 4 % (vertically) and 5.1 % (horizontally) of the radius outside the edge point, straddling the ray within 18 degrees of the vertical by (1 - 3.05 tan phi) / 2 of the width and within 45 degrees of the horizontal by (1 - cot phi) / 2 of the height; bestFit inside with the outermost corner 0.9 % of the radius inside the edge where the text fits into its slice (a one-line label may break into two lines), else outside. PowerPoint's object model reports best fit labels at their outside places and the pie keeps room for outside labels (outEnd, bestFit) but not for inEnd and ctr. Moved labels (c:manualLayout x, y) are offset from their outside place by fractions of the chart and stay inside it; a moved label clear of the pie gets a leader line from the slice's edge point, straight up or down to a label above or below it, else ending in a 5.6 pt level stroke at the label's first baseline. Legend keys (c:showLegendKey) are squares of the point's fill as in legends, the text 1.108 line heights after the inset. Bubble sizes (c:showBubbleSize) label bubbles on the right, 5.5 pt off the edge. A point label's own text (c:tx: rich text, or a cell) replaces the parts, its runs keeping their own formatting (generated/charts-details slide 6: 99.6 %); its fields (a:fld VALUE, CATEGORYNAME, SERIESNAME, PERCENTAGE, XVALUE, YVALUE, BUBBLESIZE, CELLRANGE) show the point's current values whatever text they saved ('[PERCENTAGE]' in LibreOffice's tdf125444). A label's own width (c15:layout w, a fraction of the chart) replaces the fifth it wraps at (tdf146487). Text from cells (c15:datalabelsRange) leads the parts. Best fit labels inside slices narrower than a half move sideways off the middle ray until their lines keep the same distance from both of the slice's radii, then out as far as their corners stay within reach (wide labels of slices turned in 5° steps move towards the horizontal by up to 34 px, matched within 2 px; local/piebestfit 92.4 %); one-line labels near the wrap width sit up to 4 % of the radius further in in PowerPoint.

features.title: Titles, legend and layout
features.strategy: Automatic layout of title, legend and plot area like Office; manual layouts are fractions of the chart area.
features.office: Measured against COM positions (plot area, legend entries, titles) for 35 charts: title and legend sit 6 pt from the edge, the plot area keeps 11 pt from edges, title and legend; axis labels may reach 4.5 pt into that margin (1.5 pt gap to an axis title). Horizontal legends are 1.2 times as wide as their entries ([key/2][key][key/2][text]) with equal gaps, squeeze to the chart width minus 30 pt and then wrap into balanced rows; rows are one line height plus 5.85 pt. Pies with data labels shrink by 1.785 × label size. A manual plot area layout places the inner plot area (layoutTarget inner) or, by default, the plot area with its axis labels (outer); w and h are sizes (wMode, hMode factor) or far edges (edge). Verified with generated/charts, charts-details and charts-data. Axis titles of 3D charts take their room at their axis's edge and stand centered on the plot area as on flat charts, white in the black chart area of an Office 2007 style's highest level (docx/external/powertools/CU001: "Vehicles" and "Quarter" beside a 3D bar chart). Axis titles wrap at 0.8 of the chart's width; in Word an unturned title of a vertical axis at 0.2 of it, its padding included (docx/local/atl-*: Calibri 10 titles beside charts 288 to 576 pt wide break where a line would pass 0.2 of the width less 6 pt; docx/external/libreoffice/extras-layout/tdf134146). A title without text names the chart after its single series, after none without a name: the default title (docx/external/libreoffice/extras-ooxmlexport/chart-size: Word's "Diagrammtitel", 89.8 → 97.3 %; strict 98.9 → 99.5 %, extras-layout/tdf137116 76.9 → 79.2 %). Line keys keep their size at every font size (legends of 7 to 24 pt): a 12 pt key box, the line 19.1 pt long about 12.79 pt from the entry's edge, the text at 24.31 pt; square keys scale with the line height. A legend at the side given a size of its own (c:manualLayout w, h) wraps its entries at its width less 4 pt and the key's room and shows k = min(n, ceil(height / tallest entry)) entries in equal slots of height / k, the tallest centered in its slot, all centered across (measured through COM, local/legend-manualsize; LibreOffice's tdf122765 shows 7 of 9). Keys draw markers at most half the font size and lines and marker edges at most 0.375 times it wide (local/legacy-legend* decks). A dashed line key makes every key longer: the line from 3.05 to 29.31 pt, the text at 31.5 pt (local/legacy-longkey). In Word a title without c:overlay overlays the plot as with val 1 (scratch/ WordProbes/probe_charttitle.py on LibreOffice's extras-ooxmlexport/fdo78474: the pie centred in the whole chart, below the title with val 0; fdo78474 82.2 → 99.6 %, fdo76098 88.9 → 99.8 %).

features.title: Data tables
features.strategy: Table of the series values below the plot area.
features.office: The table reaches 6 pt past the plot area's left and bottom edges; rows are L + 0.0925 s + 2.4 pt high and the name column holds the widest series name plus 1.0975 s + 2.89 pt (key 0.45 L at 0.26 L, text at 0.958 L); the plot area's left edge is the larger of the name column and the value labels, its bottom the table's top. Category labels move into the header row. The name column is at most a third of the chart's width: longer names break between words, the further lines centered under the widest, the key beside the first, and every further line makes the row a line taller with its values centered; header names break in their column less 2.7 pt on each side (local/dtable, dtable2: 99.8 and 99.3 %). Without keys the names keep 3.91 pt from the plot area. A value axis title on the left shares its room with the name column: table and plot stand where they stand without it (Word, docx/local/d3t-flat: 0.3 pt). Below 3D columns the table hangs from the floor's front edge, its columns dividing that edge, its room taken as on flat charts (docx/external/powertools/CU008, CU013: 58.6 and 62.0 → 91.5 and 92.3 %, about 5 pt wider than Word's). A deleted axis keeps its title (CU008, CU013).

features.title: Chart formatting, chart styles and colors
features.strategy: spPr and txPr of every chart element use the shared DrawingML fill, line, effect and text code; the chart style and color parts (cs) only matter where a property is not set directly. Charts without a style part are drawn in the look of their Office 2007 style (c:style, c14:style) from the theme's fill, line and effect styles, measured in PowerPoint; series effects (a:effectLst, the styles' effect styles) are SVG filters on bars, slices, areas, bubbles and markers.
features.office: PowerPoint draws bars on whole device pixels and thin lines and line chart vertices on the pixel grid (odd widths centered in a pixel); the renderer snaps the same way in slide pixel coordinates. The chart's areas (plot and chart area, legend, title) run from their bottom left corner right, up, left and down, where a dashed outline begins (Word's PDF of docx/external/libreoffice/extras-ooxmlexport/ Chart_Plot_BorderLine_Style 77.5 → 99.6 %); bars do not (Chart_BorderLine_Style). Picture fills come from the chart part's relationships; c:pictureOptions stacks them from the bar's base at their own proportions (stack) or one per c:pictureStackUnit of the value axis (stackScale), else stretches them over the bar (generated/charts-data). Verified with generated/charts, charts- more and charts-data. What a chart does not format itself shows one of the 48 Office 2007 styles (c:style, 2 without; measured with all styles, 1 to 14 series and themes whose fill, line and effect styles can be told apart), also where the chart has chart style and color parts: PowerPoint draws by them only for a title it makes up from the series' name (no c:title: the style part's 18.62 pt regular gray, generated/charts), and for Office 2016 charts (the same look and colors with and without them, local/legacy-keepstyle-column; a plot area without spPr dark in style 47, LibreOffice's tdf136754). A chart's theme override brings its own fonts (POI's aascu deck: Calibri charts in a Lucida Sans deck): style N has the color variant (N − 1) % 8 (grays, the accents in turn, one accent) and the level (N − 1) / 8. Series colors cycle through the six grays (tx1 tinted 88, 55, 78, 92, 70, 30 %) or accents with c = n / 6 + 1 cycles (one-accent styles: one per series); cycle j is shaded (before the middle) or tinted (after it) by 1.4 / (c + 1) per step in linear light, so six series are already darker. Points take fill style 1 (levels 0, 1, 4) or 3 (2, 3, 5) in their color, edges line style 1 in white (level 1) or shaded 50 % (level 4), effects effect style 2 (level 2) or 3 (3, 5). Series lines are line style 1's width times 3, 5 or 7 (level 3), markers floor(2 w + 3) pt (w the series line's own width or the style's) with an edge of line style 1 in the series color. Axis and grid lines are line style 1 in tx1 tinted 75 %; the chart area is unfilled up to level 3 (measured on a yellow slide), level 4 fills it white with a frame and tints the plot area 20 %, level 5 has a black chart area, a 95 % tx1 plot area and white text (white titles where their paragraphs have a:pPr). Text is 10 pt; titles are bold, 1.2 times the chart's text size (18 pt without one), title paragraphs without a:pPr 18 pt regular whatever the size; in Word title paragraphs whose a:pPr has a:defRPr without a size take 10 pt (probe_charttitle.py: fdo78474's "Sales" 9.96 pt bold, 18 pt without the a:pPr; fdo76098 alike). The full look needs c14:style (Office 2010) or AppVersion 12 (Office 2007); otherwise (Office 2013 and later, other programs) PowerPoint draws axis and grid lines black, level 4 plot areas in the full accent and dark gray edges black (local/legacy-* decks).

features.title: 3D charts
features.strategy: Projected 3D geometry with simple shading.
features.office: 3D charts get a box (category axis along its width, values along its height, series or the bars' row in its depth) with the back wall, side wall and floor on its far sides, gridlines over the walls and labels at the front edges (category labels turn by 45° when crowded, dates when a label and a font size do not fit, where flat charts thin them out; series labels thin out). With right-angle axes (the default of 3D columns and bars) the box is drawn in an oblique projection: front faces stay rectangles and the depth runs along (sin rotY, sin rotX) at full length. Clustered and stacked bars stand in one row depthPercent × (1 + gapDepth) bar widths deep, each bar depthPercent × its width deep and centered; standard charts, areas, lines and surfaces give every series a row of depthPercent × the category width. Without hPercent the box is as tall as the plot area's height/width ratio times its width (times floor((categories + series)/2) category widths with series rows; areas whose categories sit on the box's edges keep the height of n − 1 of their n category widths, their depth stays depthPercent of W/n: measured on 3D stacked areas of 5 and 8 categories), fitted to the plot area less the labels, which 3D charts compute like flat ones: labels centered on the edges of area and surface charts stay within the outer edges and the series axis keeps a category label gap (measured on single boxes with colored walls at 20 rotations and 22 category/series combinations, and with local/area3d, area3d3 and inset3d: 99.4 to 99.7 %). Without right-angle axes a perspective camera looks along the plot area's centre with a field of view of perspective/2 degrees spanning its height, the scene turned by rotY then rotX, and the box is fitted each way on its own: the camera's place across is where the box centred across fills the plot area's width, its place up and down where the box centred that way fills the height, and it backs off along its axis to 1.032 times the farther of both distances, keeping both places, so the box is off centre the way it does not fill (rotY 40°: 28 px left of centre, 60°: 77 px on a 1037 px wide plot area). The automatic plot area of 3D charts lies 11 pt inside the chart on every side (COM reports 7 pt left and top); a manual inner layout places the box's plot area itself. Measured with local/persp5, persp6m and persp7 (40 empty boxes with colored walls, standard and clustered, rotY 10–80°, rotX 5–45°, perspective 20–100, depth 40–400 %, seven plot areas): corners within 1 to 5 px, the decks at 98.5 to 99.5 %. With right-angle axes the box is fitted into the plot area less 1.72 pt on the left, 2.79 above, 3.34 on the right and 1.9 below, whatever the chart's size, and the value axis takes its steps from the box as large as the whole plot area; bars lie on their side, the floor standing at the category axis on the left and the side wall below them, each lit as the face it is; labels at the floor's ends (a value axis of bars) keep their outer halves in the plot area (measured with docx/local/c3o-*: bars and columns of 432 by 252 and 300 by 300 pt, rotations 0 to 40°, depths 100 and 200 %, gap depths 0 and 150 %, gap widths 150 and 300 %, the box within 0.3 pt, turned 30 and 40° within 1.5 pt; docx/external/powertools/CU007 83.0 → 93.7 %, CU012 79.3 → 90.4 %, CU001 86.2 → 90.5 %, libreoffice/extras-ooxmlexport/chart-dupe 67.8 → 91.2 %, chart-prop 79.8 → 95.5 %; external/libreoffice/chart2/bnc864396 83.4 → 95.9 %, generated/charts-3d 94.0 → 96.8 %, local/labels3d 89.4 → 93.4 %). One light shades everything (0.4 ambient plus n · (0.239, 0.357, −0.6)): fronts 1.0, tops and the floor 0.757, right sides and the side wall 0.639, sloped area and line tops in between; cylinders and cones get measured gradients (1.07 − 0.47 t², 1.13 − 0.48 t²), pyramids flat faces, cones and pyramids taper to the bar's end, the stack's end or the axis maximum (…ToMax). Areas are slabs, lines ribbons, surfaces meshes cut into the value bands (wireframes as band-colored grid and contour lines); 3D value axes get no headroom, horizontal ones keep four font sizes per interval as on flat charts (docx/external/powertools/CU012: 0 to 5 by 0.5). 3D pies are disks 0.24 of their radius thick, slices clockwise from the back at rotY, lit by a view light (tops 0.4 + 0.43 (cos rotX + sin rotX) with a small highlight, sides a gradient from the front's light, cut faces of exploded slices lit from the right); exploded pies fit as a disk as wide as their farthest slice. Data labels: on bars beyond the end face, centered on the front face (ctr, inEnd, inBase on it), on areas halfway up their band on the front, beside the points of lines, on pies inside the top as far out as they fit (outEnd beyond the rim), a labelled pie fitting at 89 % of its size; horizontal value axes keep a label and three font sizes per interval. Thick walls (c:thickness, a percentage of the box's smaller side: 10 % of a 0.82 high box reach 0.083 of its width) are slabs beside, below and behind the box that take their room in the fit, carry the labels on their outer faces and the gridlines across their front and end faces (generated/charts-data slide 6: 94.8 %, 57.7 % before). Bars without fill and line draw nothing, their faces unshaded. Checked with generated/charts-3d (92.8 %, 18 slides; 88 % before the perspective fit) and local/persp to persp4 (97.0 to 99.5 %). 3D surfaces (measured with local/surf3d, surf3d2, surfbox and surfwalls: single cells of known slope, folded cells, 16 grids and walls seen from 13 sides, 93.7 to 98.5 %): the box is ⌊(categories + series − 1)/2⌋ category widths high, each cell folds along the diagonal with the larger sum, facets are lit 0.821 + 0.313 n·(0.768, 0.182, −0.614) for the normal as the camera sees it in perspective and 0.641 + 0.380 n·(0.616, 0.491, −0.616) in the box with right-angle axes, their walls 0.4 + 0.75 n·(0.572, 0.586, −0.574) for the inner normal (seen by the camera, or in the box with right-angle axes); at rotY 0 the side wall stands on the left. Views from other sides (local/backview, rotY 100° to 300°, 95.1 %): seen from behind (the camera beyond the middle of the box's depth) the back wall stands at the near end of the data and the floor's labels run along its near edge; the vertical axis always stands at the box's left end (x = 0), on whichever of its two edges lies outside on the screen, from behind on the right where its labels take no room; labels along a floor edge within 34° of the horizontal stand under it, else beside it away from the box (categories under at 27° and 32°, beside at 36°; series under at 12°, beside at 41°). Wireframes (local/wire and wire2, single cells with bands every 2): grid pieces in their band's line, a level piece on a band boundary in the band below, contour lines in the line of the band below (generated/charts-3d slide 13: 87.7 %, 76.3 % before). Category labels under the floor get 0.94 of their categories' share of its edge's width on the screen, wrap at their spaces when they do not fit and turn by 45° when a word alone does not (local/wrap3d: clustered columns 300 to 840 pt wide, names of one to three words, turned 20°, 300° and 330°: 96.3 %). Known deviations: the topmost contour of wireframe cells rising like a plane, which PowerPoint draws in the band above (not in saddles, whose contours match), and labels on the edge of fitting under an edge rising 32° (local/backview slide 6), which PowerPoint wraps where the box's size with single-line labels lets them fit.

features.title: Trendlines and error bars
features.strategy: Regression fits (linear, exponential, logarithmic, polynomial, power, moving average) and error bars.
features.office: Trendlines: linear, exponential, logarithmic, polynomial (order 2-6), power and moving average, with forward/backward forecast and fixed intercepts, drawn 1.5 pt dotted in the series color by default and clipped to the plot area. Equation and R squared labels show coefficients rounded to 4 decimals; the block is vertically centered on the trendline's end, its right edge 8.8 pt left of it (measured). Legend entries follow the series; a dashed key line (the dotted trendline's, or a series') gives every entry a longer key of 31.5 pt (a solid trendline does not). Error bars: fixed value, percentage, standard error, custom values and standard deviation (around the mean of all values, like Office), 4.5 pt caps; they extend the value axis.

features.title: Shapes drawn on charts
features.strategy: Shapes anchored in relative or absolute chart coordinates; drawn with the normal shape code.
features.office: A chart's drawing part (c:userShapes) anchors shapes by fractions of the chart frame (relSizeAnchor from/to) or by a corner and a size (absSizeAnchor); the shapes are DrawingML shapes, groups, pictures and connectors like on slides, their text without a size takes the chart's text properties, else 10 pt (measured with generated/charts-more).

features.title: Pivot chart settings
features.strategy: Field buttons are not shown in presentations; pivot formats apply like data point formats.
features.office: Pivot sources, pivot formats and field button options do not change the picture: PowerPoint shows pivot charts like other charts, with the formats stored on the series and points, and without field buttons.

features.title: Office 2016 charts (chartex)
features.description: Waterfall, treemap, sunburst, histogram, Pareto, box and whisker, funnel and region map.
features.strategy: Each type needs its own layout (treemap squarify, sunburst rings, histogram binning, box plot statistics); region maps use the geography data cached in the file. Check whether mc:Fallback contains a usable picture.
features.office: PowerPoint saves Office 2016 charts as mc:AlternateContent (Requires cx1/cx2) with a picture of the chart in mc:Fallback, which is drawn (generated/charts-more slides 6 and 7: 98.5 %). Files without the picture get the chart laid out natively (the chartex Choice is taken only then): a classic frame built from it (title, legend, axes) with layout rules measured on probe decks of 130 to 450 pt wide charts (local chartex, chartex-p1 … p4, chartex-pareto: 96–99 %): the plot area 6 pt from the edges and 4.25 pt below the title's line, axis labels 6.9 pt off it, category labels in a row, staggered up to 1.3 slots, turned by −30° up to 1.65 and −60° up to 2.15 slots, else upright; legends packed in rows of at most 80 % of the chart; histogram bins of Scott's width to two significant digits without axis headroom; waterfall totals and connectors; funnels; Pareto lines on a percentage axis; box plots (exclusive or inclusive quartiles, 1.5 IQR whiskers, outliers, means); squarified treemaps with overlapping or banner labels; sunbursts sorted by size with radial, wrapped labels. Region maps (local chartex-map … map4 at 300 to 900 pt: 98.4–99.9 %) are drawn from their geography cache (raw deflated XML whose rings are Bing point compressed in the base64url alphabet) in Robinson's projection, 1.5 % wider than defined, fitted beside a color scale legend (interpolated in linear light) with the map's credits below; like PowerPoint's own pictures of such files, every region is gray, as the cache does not tell which region a data point names. Not reproduced: the ellipsis PowerPoint puts on long category labels in very short charts.

features.title: Saved SmartArt drawing
features.strategy: Draw the shapes from the diagram's drawing part like normal shapes.
features.office: PowerPoint stores the laid-out shapes of every SmartArt in a drawing part (dsp:drawing), so files saved by PowerPoint need no SmartArt layout engine. The drawing is not complete, though: PowerPoint draws the text in the color the color definition gives the shape's style label (txFillClrLst, by the presentation point's presStyleIdx/presStyleCnt) where the drawing keeps the quick style's fontRef color (white text on the white boxes of the outline color schemes otherwise); it formats text by the layout's list style (Office 2016 extension dgm1612:lstStyle, by the depth of the text's data point, which the drawing loses: the layout tree tells which points each shape shows); and a 3D quick style's scene (styleDef/scene3d: camera with zoom and light rig) turns the whole diagram about its center, which the drawing does not keep either (Camera.Pivot, Camera.Zoom). A text rectangle (dsp:txXfrm) stands where the shape stands, turned by the shape's rotation plus its own (rot 90 with a text rot of -90 keeps the text of a turned chevron upright). Measured with all 159 layouts (98.8 %) and all 38 color definitions and 14 quick styles on a process (98.6 %, the rest 3D materials). A drawing part without shapes counts as missing: PowerPoint lays the diagram out anew (LibreOffice's SmartArt test decks, whose drawings are emptied).

features.title: SmartArt data model
features.strategy: The text and structure of the nodes; needed for editing and for files without a drawing part.
features.office: PowerPoint keeps the laid-out shapes in the drawing part (smartart.drawing); the data model adds the diagram's own formatting: dgm:bg (fill and effects, e.g. a shadow) is drawn as a rectangle over the frame behind the shapes and dgm:whole (line and effects) on top of them (measured with generated/smartart: 99.2 %). The diagram is an element of its own sized like its frame, which animations of the whole diagram change; every shape carries the model id of its presentation point, which per-shape animations target (p:graphicEl/a:dgm with the drawing shape's model id; ids of data nodes or transitions animate nothing in PowerPoint, measured with its video export), and a:dgm bldStep=bg targets the background and outline. Checked against PowerPoint's video of generated/smartart slide 3 (background, a node fading, a node and its connector flying in, the rest appearing): 96.8 % (tools/Fidelity animate). The node structure (points, connections, presentation variables) only serves the layout engine for files without a drawing part (smartart.layout).

features.title: SmartArt layout engine
features.strategy: Only for SmartArt without a saved drawing (files from other producers): layout algorithms (linear, snake, cycle, hierarchy, pyramid …) with constraints and rules.
features.office: Only for SmartArt without a saved drawing (PowerPoint 2007 and other producers; PowerPoint itself always saves one). The layout tree is instantiated for the data model (all 159 built-in layouts match PowerPoint's presentation points; pos functions with an axis take the first selected point's position). Constraints: a node's own values first, those its ancestors give over them (the nearest last; equalizing and defaulting constraints do not count); a node showing a node's text counts as one for ptType; sp given to all descendants skips the lines laying out the owner's own point; a list's lte and gte bounds on other nodes hold where they stand and again until they hold together, a node's bounds on itself at the end, a value only bounds give follows them unless fitting fixed it, bounds on user variables hold nothing, and bounds between font sizes lower the larger one after fitting (an unset size being the default 36 pt), bounds with a negative factor hold nothing; a constraint without value or reference gives 0 only where nothing else gives a value, in the node's own list only where nothing before it does (HorizontalActionList's titles, h <= 0.3 w then h: 0.3 w high; arrow5's ring of eight, sibSp then sibSp <= 0.1 h: spaced 0); edges, centers and sizes are derived from each other with their offsets, references to a placed node read its laid-out box (sizes without its own offset), a root's child taller than the diagram as high as it (a square one keeping its shape), references to a node no instance of which exists take the value the list would give it, and every node evaluates its list again once its parent's algorithm gives it its box. Rules lower their targets toward val, or toward fact times what the target's value refers to; a lin node's font size rule also applies while a child is larger across the line than the node, strictly (LibreOffice's smartart-dir: hList1's columns at 31 pt in a frame 182.5 pt high, 56 -> 99.8 %), the children measured once the bounds their own lists set have settled (process3's descriptions below titles h <= 0.4 w: the row keeps its width and the titles their 34 pt; LibreOffice's smartart-accent-process 72.1 -> 98.6 %). Text whose runs all have sizes of their own keeps them and is not fitted; its margins follow that size, while boxes sized from its font size keep the size the constraints gave (LibreOffice's fill-color-list: titles of 18 pt, descriptions 1.22 x 65 high, 51 -> 100 %). Algorithms: composite (the room of all its children's boxes, invisible leaves included, a child taking its box keeping the bounds the composite sets between its width and height by giving up room across, centered, a lin child without a size taking its box; ar keeps its box while references see its constraint size; a composite root's drawing centered in the frame), lin (its rules on the children's length first, by halving to within a point of the room, font size rules in whole points, then uniform shrinking, a shrunk composite taking its content's room, along and, without a size of its own, across; a lin child whose children all stay narrower across its line taking their room; the row as long as the farthest a child reaches; sp only between neighbors without a spacer node; the row aligned in the node and each child across it; fallback 2D laid out at the own size and scaled; a tree alone on the line centered by itself; children's subtrees evaluated for its box before they are measured), snake (rules in 32nds of the way, fixed and balanced breakpoints, cells in place by their box and the grid aligned by the room their shapes take, short rows from their start unless off ctr, each row alignOff further, rows growing from grDir, cells never grown, connectors with a size spacing the cells, line gaps following the placed cells they refer to), cycle (the circle as small as keeps each two neighbors' outlines, an ellipse's or a box's as laid out, not turned along the path, sibSp apart along the line between them, each next but one at least touching, and the ring sp from the middle shape; measured with arrow5 and arrow1 at 3 to 8 nodes and sibSp from -0.9 to 0.3 times their width, 26 rings within 0.2 %: three nodes never closer than touching, seven spaced by the box their turned neighbors would not have; the node's rules in 32nds before shrinking; a ring with room to spare spreading out up to its own diameter, the shapes keeping their size; curved connectors as circular arrows or arcs over their span, padded along the arc), hierRoot/hierChild (subtrees as close as the shapes lying side by side allow, sibSp apart; rows lined up with the root's box and hung sp beyond its shapes; parents centered over their first and last child's head; assistants on a level of their own, in a horizontal chart a column of their own half their sibSp above the line; bent connectors; texts' values evaluated again as drawn), pyra (text rectangles 0.65 of a level's width, the apex's whole box), connectors between the shapes they join (named ends found inside the transitions' nodes, the diagram's own, the siblings named or the one node of that name; straight ones between named points, an automatic end at the middle of its node's side nearest to the named one, the radial points where a cycle's circle meets the nodes, or a center; placed again once laid out where they join nodes outside their parent; connDist made equal at the shortest; curved ones with a diameter along their circle between their named points, a diameter of connDist following it, negative ones counterclockwise, one from a node back to itself in a cycle closing the ring short of the node by 0.09°, a band without heads in a cycle a quarter of its width further in; stems alone 0.6 of the height without heads; lines without a height having none). Shapes turned by their rot take the size whose turned bounds are their box; a composite root is centered where its drawing fits the frame with its own connectors. Text fitting: every line its font's height times the line spacing, paragraphs apart by their space after, within the geometry's text rectangle and the margins (a boxless text node within the shape showing it); 36 pt where no constraint gives a size; font sizes in whole points, secondary sizes by their own rules, equ groups at their smallest; heights growing in sixteenths as far as the parent has room and lte bounds allow, widths growing in 32nds of the way to a rule's limit; descendants' text at the top level unless bullets start at its depth; the diagram laid out again with the pinned values. The output writes the shapes the way PowerPoint writes its drawing (text nodes' text taken by shapes showing the same data, styles and colors by label); a data point's own formatting (dgm:pt/dgm:spPr) colors the shape showing its text, unless that shape hides its geometry, before the shape's presentation point's (LibreOffice's smartart-cycle-matrix: 75.3 to 98.7 %); bulleted text hangs by 4.5 pt per size class (4.5 pt below 12 pt, 9 below 16, 13.5 below 20, 18 below 28, then 22.5; measured on PowerPoint's drawings of one diagram at 22 sizes). Measured against PowerPoint's drawings of the 159 layouts: 1349 of 1455 shapes within 1 %, 146 diagrams exact, 745 of 823 font sizes (151 shapes and 12 diagrams before this engine work); against generated decks of snake, picture, cycle, radial and hierarchy layouts at 1 to 8 nodes: 541 of 542, 550 of 594, 311 of 320, 412 of 427 and 578 of 690 shapes; rendered with the drawings removed 94.1 % (38.5 % before), all color definitions and quick styles on a process 97.9 %. Known deviations (only for diagrams saved without their drawing): HorizontalActionList's description boxes, which PowerPoint keeps at one height for two or more nodes that depends on the frame alone (250.3 pt in 840 x 460, 133 in 840 x 300, 285.1 in 600 x 460; one node fills the composite), AscendingPictureAccentProcess's drawing, which PowerPoint shrinks by 0.74 to 0.93 for 2 to 5 nodes and centers by its outline, BendingPictureBlocks' pictures overhanging their composites, cycle3's long curves, NameandTitleOrganizationalChart's names narrower than their constraint and radial2's ring (2 % smaller), each within 1 to 7 % (sa_all: 13 of 159 layouts not exact), and process3 with a description longer than its box, for which PowerPoint lowers the titles' font size the description's follows and grows the box, where the engine lets the description overflow.

features.title: SmartArt styles and color definitions
features.strategy: Part of the layout engine path.
features.office: Color definitions: each style label lists fill, line, effect and text colors applied in turn (repeat), spread from the first to the last color (span: shape i of n at i/(n-1)) or there and back (cycle: 2i/n up to the middle, then back), spread colors written as the first with the HSL and alpha differences added (hueOff, satOff, lumOff, alphaOff; hue clockwise unless hueDir=ccw); PowerPoint's offsets match HSL differences computed with the sRGB transfer function for tint and shade. The index is the presentation point's presStyleIdx of presStyleCnt: shapes showing the same data points share one, decorations count each. Text color from txFillClrLst, else the quick style's fontRef. The quick style's scene3d turns the whole diagram (3d5 to 3d9 styles); its labels give style references, sp3d and light rigs, which the drawing keeps; its labels' text properties (dgm:txPr, the 3d9 style's a:sp3d extrusion) go into the text body's a:bodyPr. Applied to diagrams with a saved drawing (smartart.drawing) and to those the engine lays out (smartart.layout writes style references, color list colors, 3D properties and text properties per label like PowerPoint's drawings; all color definitions and quick styles on a process with the drawings removed: 95.7 %). Built-in color definitions leave txLinClrLst and txEffectClrLst empty; they are not applied.

features.title: Transition timing and sound
features.strategy: Duration from spd or p14:dur; advance on click and/or after advTm; optional sound.

spec.title: Slide Transition for a Slide Layout

features.title: Classic transitions
features.strategy: Two stacked slide layers with SVG masks, transforms and opacity; WebGL for the 3D ones.
features.office: Compared with PowerPoint's videos (tools/Fidelity transitions): 95.2 % over generated/transitions-classic. Masks with the soft edges PowerPoint draws for wipes, splits, strips, shapes and wheels; push, cover, uncover, comb, zoom and newsflash with PowerPoint's easing; blinds and checkerboard turn bands and tiles over in 3D as PowerPoint plays them since 2013; dissolve and random bars use random patterns of their own.

features.title: Office 2010 transitions
features.strategy: The slides (or their content and backgrounds apart) rasterized into textures and drawn in a WebGL scene with PowerPoint's camera; particle-like ones (vortex, shred, honeycomb, glitter) as many small tiles.
features.office: All of them, compared with PowerPoint's videos: 83.4 % over generated/transitions-2010. Prism, cube, box, orbit, flip, switch, gallery, doors, window, ferris wheel, conveyor, pan, fly through, warp, reveal and flash as WebGL scenes whose poses and timing are fitted frame by frame; ripple as a growing soft circle; glitter, vortex, shred and honeycomb as turning tiles and particles with PowerPoint's timing, their random patterns differing from PowerPoint's. Written as mc:AlternateContent with a p:fade fallback.

features.title: Office 2013 transitions
features.strategy: The slides as WebGL meshes deformed per vertex (hinged, curled, gathered, crumpled, shattered, folded).
features.office: All presets with invX, compared with PowerPoint's videos: 83.9 % over generated/transitions-2013. Fall over, drape, curtains, wind, prestige, crush, fracture, peel off, page curl (single and double), airplane and origami as meshes bent, folded and moved with keyframes measured from the videos; airplane and origami fold into simplified shapes.

features.title: Morph
features.strategy: Match objects between the two slides (same name, names starting with !!, similar content), then interpolate position, size, rotation, fill and geometry; words or characters for text.
features.office: Compared with PowerPoint's video: 96.8 % over generated/transitions-morph (objects, words, characters, !! names). Shapes paired by name move, grow and turn at PowerPoint's ease, the old one fading out over the new one; text by words or characters moves unit by unit. Written as mc:AlternateContent with p:fade in mc:Fallback.

features.title: Timing tree
features.strategy: A JS timing engine for the SMIL-like time containers (par, seq, excl): click sequences, with/after previous, triggers on shapes and media bookmarks, fill, repeat, auto-reverse, acceleration and deceleration.
features.office: Checked against PowerPoint's own video of the slides (tools/Fidelity animate: slideshow 99.9 %, smartart 99.9 %, animations-charts 99.6 %, animations-text 100.0 %, animations-gallery 99.7 % of frames). Acceleration and deceleration follow a smoothstep speed curve (measured on six accel/decel pairs). A behaviour without fill of its own reverts when it ends, a set without duration holds; formulas take the current values (ppt_x, ppt_y …, not #ppt_x) as they are when their behaviour begins, a behaviour ending just then with its end (Bounce Out's fall and bounces build on each other). Text built letter by letter or word by word (p:iterate lt, wd; el, the default, animates the whole target): the shape's background first for the effect's duration when the build animates it (bldP animBg) and for emphases, then every letter or word (blanks are none) with the whole effect, tmPct of the effect's duration or tmAbs apart; a group after the previous effect starts when the groups before it end (the stored delay is the editor's guess, which iterated text outlasts). After effects and sounds (p:subTnLst): sameClick ones when their effect begins or ends as their condition says, nextClick ones (dim, hide on next click) when the next effect of the sequence begins. Containers repeat (repeatCount, repeatDur); indefinite repeats go on after their step until the end of the slide, or until the next click with an onNext end condition (checked live). A container ends with its last child (endSync all), with its first under endSync first; an exclusive container (p:excl) stops the child playing when another begins. Interactive sequences (triggers) play a click group per click on their shape or bookmark; once played (endSync all) the next click starts them again (restart whenNotActive), not with restart never. Effects with fill=remove rewind when done, tmFilter remaps progress, p14:bounceEnd swings about the end as a damped spring over its share of the duration (fitted on five videos). PowerPoint's video clock advances whole milliseconds per frame (33 ms at 30 fps) within a step while steps follow the video's frames; the player's frame mode does the same.

spec.title: Slide Timing Information for a Slide Layout

features.title: Animation targets
features.strategy: Targets are shapes, paragraph or character ranges and chart or SmartArt parts, so the rendered output must keep those addressable.
features.office: Shapes, paragraph ranges (p:pRg), character ranges (p:charRg; their text is drawn character by character), backgrounds (p:bg), SmartArt shapes (a:dgm), chart parts (a:chart: series, categories, points, background), the letters and words of text built by iteration (data-c, data-w), sounds (p:sndTgt, played with their effect) and ink (p:inkTgt, and p:spTgt of an ink content part, which PowerPoint writes: the ink is drawn with its shape id; checked with a fade on two ink drawings) are addressable.

features.title: Animation behaviours
features.strategy: Attribute names (ppt_x, ppt_y, ppt_w, ppt_h, style.rotation, style.opacity, style.visibility, fillcolor …) map to properties of the rendered elements; animEffect filters (fade, wipe, barn, blinds, circle …) become SVG masks; motion paths are relative path strings.
features.office: Formulas use ppt_x, ppt_y, ppt_w, ppt_h (the property's current value as the behaviour begins, used by exit effects such as Fly Out and Bounce Out) besides #ppt_x … (the value before the animation). Motion paths move at a speed even in the path's own units (fractions of the slide's width and height), not on the screen (measured with a circle path: 1.1 px against 7.6 px). Filters (measured frame by frame with PowerPoint's videos of every filter and direction, entrance and exit): every point of the shape's drawn bounds (its outline included) has a moment u at which the edge passes it, in the bounds' own proportions: the distance from the starting side (wipe; blinds in 6 bands; checkerboard in 6 x 6 cells, odd rows half a cell over), from the middle (box, circle reaching the corners, diamond, plus, barn), the angle from 12 o'clock (wedge both ways, wheel per spoke), the diagonal of a 16 x 16 block grid (strips, u = d/31). The edge is a linear ramp 0.14 wide from just before u = 0 to just past u = 1. Exits hide what the edge passes; blinds, checkerboard and strips play their entrance backwards instead. Dissolve shows one-pixel specks at the pace of the average of three random numbers (an S curve), random bars one-pixel lines at a measured pace. The player draws all of them as SVG masks (gradients, fans, a thresholded noise image) on the shape's drawing, so outlines past the shape's box stay; groups get a CSS mask over their box. Color animations work in RGB and HSL (to, by; the hue turns the way dir says whatever the sign of by, Complementary Color 2). Text formatting (style.fontWeight, style.fontStyle, style.textDecorationUnderline, style.fontFamily) shows the text laid out anew in the real faces, as PowerPoint does: the converter draws it in every formatting the timing gives it, per paragraph or, for text built letter by letter, per letter (lined up with the letter it stands for); style.fontSize scales the text about its anchor and ends in the text laid out at that size. fill.on gives a shape without fill the animated fill; stroke.on, fill.opacity, stroke.opacity, stroke.weight, ppt_r and imageData.grayscale (VML-era names PowerPoint's presets do not use) are applied too. Effects of an iterated build animate the background first, the font size scales only the text (generated/animations-gallery: 99.7 % of 373 video frames over 12 slides of PowerPoint's effect gallery).

features.title: Build lists
features.strategy: Build text by paragraph and level, charts by series or category, SmartArt by node.
features.office: SmartArt builds (a:bldDgm one, lvlOne, lvlAtOnce) are written as effects per drawing shape (p:graphicEl with a:dgm id = the shape's model id, bldStep bg for the diagram's background); the player animates each shape of the diagram on its own (checked with tools/Fidelity animate on generated/smartart). Chart builds (a:bldChart series, category, seriesEl, categoryEl) are effects per a:chart step: gridLegend (everything but the data), series, category, ptInSeries, ptInCategory, with seriesIdx -3/-4 and categoryIdx -3/-4 where they do not apply (PowerPoint keeps them so; its object model refuses chart builds of modern charts). PowerPoint animates a series or category as one: a wipe runs over the box around all its bars, labels and markers; a line segment builds with the category it ends at. The chart marks its parts (data-ser in plot order, data-pt), the player animates their union (generated/animations-charts: 99.5 % of 103 video frames). Builds of legacy OLE charts (p:bldOleChart) animate the whole object, which is drawn from its picture.

features.title: Effect presets
features.description: presetClass, presetID and presetSubtype on p:cTn.
features.strategy: The timing tree already contains the behaviours; presets only name PowerPoint's effects (Fade, Fly In, Wipe …) for the editor.

features.title: Media control and bookmarks
features.strategy: Play, pause and stop commands and media bookmarks as timing events.
features.office: Media nodes (p:audio, p:video, cMediaNode) give volume and mute, showWhenStopped 0 (the shape hides in the show while the medium is not playing), numSld (it plays on across that many slides), fullScrn (a video fills the slide, centered, while it plays) and isNarration (narration media stay silent when the show plays without narrations); p:cmd plays, pauses, resumes, stops and seeks them; bookmarks (p14:bmkTgt) start trigger sequences when playback reaches them; sounds of effects (p:sndTgt in the effect's p:subTnLst, begin of the effect) play with the effect. What was done during a recorded show (p14:showEvtLst in the slide's extLst: play, pause, resume, stop, seek of media, clicks on triggers) replays at its times from the start of the slide's timeline when the show uses its timings. Checked live in the browser with probe decks (times within 10 ms).

features.title: Animated pictures
features.strategy: Play the embedded animations of 3D models in the slide show with our own glTF renderer: skins, node transforms (linear, step and cubic spline keys) and morph targets, posed at the effect's progress.
features.office: A 3D model's embedded animations (a3danim:embedAnim with aanim:animPr, a3danim:posterFrame) play in the slide show only through the slide's timing: PowerPoint adds a Scene effect (presetID 100, emph, with the slide's start, repeatCount indefinite) whose p:anim takes attrName embeddedN from 0 to 1: the glTF file's animation N - 1 (not embedAnim's animId) over its whole length, stretched to the effect's duration; without the effect the model stands still at its poster frame (measured with PowerPoint's videos). animPr (length, count, auto, offset, st, end) and the poster frame describe the playback in PowerPoint's own views; the document shows the poster frame, as printed. PowerPoint offers only skeletal animations: a model whose animations move plain nodes or morph targets gets none. Before its first key a cubic spline is, in PowerPoint, that key's in-tangent. Checked with generated/models (99.8 % of PowerPoint's video frames) and a rigged fox (local, 99.7 %).

features.title: Recorded laser pointer
features.strategy: Replay recorded laser pointer movements with the narration.
features.office: A recorded laser pointer (p14:laserTraceLst in the slide's extLst) replays in the slide show when narrations play (showPr showNarration; without showPr PowerPoint plays them, measured): the pointer, in p14:laserClr of the show settings (red by default), follows every trace (p14:tracePtLst) from its first to its last point, at the points' times (ST_UniversalTimeOffset, milliseconds without a unit) from the start of the slide's timeline after the transition, moving straight between the recorded points (x, y in EMU from the slide's top left corner). PowerPoint draws nothing of it on the slide itself. Checked with generated/laser (slide unchanged; replay positions checked in the browser).

features.title: Slide show player
features.strategy: Navigation by click, keys and swipe; advance timings; loop and kiosk mode; full screen; presenter view with notes.
features.office: Verified with generated/slideshow (navigation, timings, loop, kiosk, presenter view).

features.title: Hyperlinks and action settings
features.strategy: Links for URLs and files; ppaction:// actions (jump to slide, next, previous, first, last, end show, custom show) handled by the player; hover actions and sounds.
features.office: Hyperlinked text is drawn in the theme's hyperlink color unless ahyp:hlinkClr says to keep the text color. Mouse-over actions (a:hlinkHover on shapes) run when the pointer enters the shape during the show. Mouse-over actions on text (a:hlinkMouseOver) run when the pointer enters the text during the show, like a shape's a:hlinkHover. highlightClick, invalidUrl and tgtFrame do not change the picture. Programs, macros and OLE verbs are deliberately not run from a web page.

features.title: Summary, section and slide zoom
features.strategy: Draw the zoom's picture and link it to the target slide or section; the player zooms in and back out.
features.office: Zoom objects (slide, section and summary zooms) are drawn from their mc:Fallback pictures, linked to their slides (local/zoom: 99.6 %). In the slide show a click zooms into the target: the view closes in on the zoom's frame until the slide, growing out of it, fills the screen, over transitionDur (an even zoom in scale with a sine ease; without transitionDur the slide's own transition plays). With returnToParent (the default) the show zooms back out to the zoom's slide after the target slide or the last slide of the section. The zoom's motion is not measured against PowerPoint: its video export follows the slide order and a live show would need a real click.

features.title: Comments (classic)
features.strategy: Optional comment markers and a side panel.
features.office: Classic comments (p:cmLst, authors from commentAuthors.xml with their color index, replies joined to their thread through p15:threadingInfo/p15:parentCm) are never drawn by PowerPoint, neither on slides nor in the slide show. The document lists the threads below each slide on request (the player's comment button or C) with markers labelled with the author's initials and index at p:pos, which counts 1/576 inch from the slide's top left corner (PowerPoint's master units). Times are shown as stored. Checked with generated/comments.

features.title: Modern comments, reactions and tasks
features.strategy: Optional threaded comments in a side panel.
features.office: Modern comments (p188:cmLst, authors from authors.xml, linked from the slide by p188:commentRel) are listed with their replies, status (resolved, closed), reactions (p223: the emoji with the reacting authors) and tasks (assignees, start and due date, progress and title from the comment's attributes, or replayed from the p228 history without undone events). Markers sit at p188:pos in EMU from the top left corner of the anchor: the slide, or the shape that ac:deMkLst or ac:txMkLst names by id or creationId. Created times are UTC and shown in the viewer's time zone. Checked with generated/comments; PowerPoint draws none of it on slides.

features.title: VML drawings
features.strategy: Only for very old converted files and controls: prefer the DrawingML fallback (the picture of an OLE object or control); a VML renderer is a separate project.
features.office: PowerPoint 2007 saved the pictures of OLE objects and ActiveX controls only in a VML drawing part of the slide: p:oleObj and p:control name their VML shape (spid), whose v:imagedata (o:relid or r:id, croptop/bottom/left/right as fractions or 1/65536ths) holds the picture; later versions add a DrawingML picture in p:pic and write the VML choice without any picture (mc:Choice Requires=v, so the fallback is taken). Without a DrawingML picture the document draws the VML one in the object's frame, a control at the place its VML shape's style gives (PowerPoint does the same: measured with a VML picture differing from the object, generated/legacy-vml 99.8 %). HTML-like VML (unclosed br) is closed before parsing. Slides hold no other VML content.

features.title: HTML output
features.strategy: One self-contained HTML document (or folder) per presentation: slides as fixed-size containers at 96 dpi, scaled to the viewport; images and fonts embedded or next to it; no external dependencies.
features.office: Every corpus deck converts to one self-contained document.

features.title: Text measurement and line breaking
features.strategy: Shape text with HarfBuzz using the actual font files, break lines like PowerPoint (UAX 14 plus Office's rules), justify and position every line ourselves; the browser only draws the positioned runs.
features.office: Measured with the text-snap calibration deck: glyph advances, kerning and letter spacing are each rounded to master units (1/8 pt, half up); kerning uses the legacy 'kern' table (GDI pairs). Fonts without one are kerned from GPOS only when they are PostScript (CFF) or variable fonts (measured: Bahnschrift, Segoe UI Variable, Sitka and embedded Gotham and Wix Madefor Display are kerned; Gabriola, Javanese Text and Yu Mincho, static TrueType with GPOS pairs, are not). Within a format run the glyph origins are rounded to whole pixels (half up) from the run's exact start; a new format run starts exactly. Baselines sit on whole pixels counted from the top of the text area (box top plus inset, anchor offset included). Glyphs are drawn unhinted with 8×4 samples per pixel. From 30 pixels per em text is therefore drawn as glyph outlines (paths defined once per document, placed with use) at the exact positions, with the text transparent on top for selection and search; browser text would sit on whole-pixel baselines and be hinted. PowerPoint samples coverage at the top-left of 8 × 4 sub-pixels, Chromium at the centers of 4 sub-rows: outlines are shifted by 1/16 and 1/8 pixel to see the same edges. Verified with generated/text- metrics, text-snap and text-basic.

features.title: Font resolution and fallback
features.strategy: Find installed and embedded fonts, metric-compatible substitutes (Carlito for Calibri, Liberation for Arial and Times New Roman) and Office cloud fonts (Aptos); subset and embed them as WOFF2, so the browser draws with exactly the font we measured.
features.office: PowerPoint renders text from 30 pixels per em on unhinted (cap height and x-height exactly as designed), below that hinted with crisp horizontal edges on whole-pixel baselines (22 pt hinted, 23 pt smooth at 96 dpi). Large text is emitted as glyph outlines, so the viewer needs no fonts for it; small text, color fonts, synthesized bold or italic and glyphs missing from the font are left to the browser, whose hinted rendering matches PowerPoint's small text closely (Arial exactly); fonts the browser cannot find by name are embedded for these runs. Installed fonts without a typographic family whose family name holds a weight or width are named by their faces' full names (local()): Windows groups them by the rest of the name, so Chrome drew "Franklin Gothic Medium" in Franklin Gothic Demi and found "Franklin Gothic Demi", "Eras Medium ITC" or "OCR A Extended" not at all (Times New Roman); all 30 such families on this machine are their own faces so. Verified with generated/text-basic, text-eastasian, text-more and probe/font.

features.title: Fidelity measurement
features.strategy: Reference renderings from PowerPoint (COM, Windows only) against screenshots of our HTML (headless Chromium), compared slide by slide; the scores show where to work next.
features.office: tools/Fidelity generates the corpus, renders references with PowerPoint and scores every deck.
